title: Terrific light for video
text:
I have been using Neewer products for over 5 years. My first purchase was a cheap fluorescent ring light in early 2017 and have seen considerable improvement in both the variety and quality of products they offer while remaining reasonably priced. I have purchased several lights, a camera slider, tripod dolly, lens filters, etc. and everything has lived up to my expectations and I still use all of it. Nothing has ever broken or stopped working.

This light comes with the light unit, a mounting bracket to attach it to a light stand, a DC power converter, a power cord, a soft carrying case with plenty of foam padding, and an instruction manual.
It took only a couple of minutes to set up right out of the box. It was also easy to install the app on my phone and connect with the light via Bluetooth. The app allows the light to be controlled remotely and is intuitive and easy to use.

I tested this light this morning and plan on using it to light a video this evening. I had no problem using the Android app to control the brightness, color temperature, and effects. It can also be controlled manually via the knobs and buttons on the back of the unit. I tried using the Sony NP-F-style batteries (it holds 2) and the AC power. Each worked equally well though I would want more than one set of batteries if I were using them for a shoot. On the brightest setting, the light is quite bright and could be used as a key light. It can be dimmed for use as a fill or backlight. However, because it is a panel of lights, it cannot be used as a focused spotlight. The panel cover is a diffuser that softens the light considerably. It is built-in and not removable.

Overall I would say this is a terrific light and worth the price. Easily 5 stars.

title: Strong opening; a tiresome slog therafter
text: At least one reviewer on this page characterizes SIASL as "juvenile".  I'd have to say that pretty well sums up the greater part of this book.  In its day SIASL may have shone a light on the prevailing counter-cultural trends in American society.  And it may have been cutting edge sci-fi.  As such, it is perhaps of historical interest to those who might be interested.  To the casual reader, however, it's a pretty tiresome read.  The opening section, which deals with the protagonist's arrival on earth and initial adaptation thereto is quite interesting and well-paced.  The greater part of what remains, however, is given over to endless anthropological/religious historical musings of one sort or another, interlaced with endlessly banal descriptions of life in the Utopian commune our hero founds.  Much of this material fails either to titillate the reader's senses or to stimulate his/her intellect.  It reads like one long (LONG) masturbatory exercise on the author's part -- well-written, in fairness, but rather...juvenile.  As for the novel's ending: you'll spot it coming a mile away.  In the final analysis: SIASL is a creature of its times, ill-suited to our own.

title: Panasonic goes out of its way to avoid rewarding loyalty
text:
First, my refurbished units work just fine - no problems there, at least not so far.

I've had earlier versions of these Panasonic phones, and they work well. Compared to earlier versions, there was one pleasant surprise and two unpleasant ones.

The good, compared to earlier versions - the display is easy to see. I got this set for my parents, so that they could have phones all over the house, and the display makes them easy to use.

The bad - first, they took away the intercom button. Instead of just pushing the intercom button and then selecting which handset to call, you have to select menu, then scroll down several steps, then select intercom, and then scroll down to pick the handset to call. The steps are slow - every time, the menu takes a noticeable amount of time to appear, as does the list of handsets. So, the entire process is at least 3 times as long and cumbersome as before. They took an easy feature and made it painful.

Second, every single time Panasonic comes out with a new version of these phones, they go out of their way to make sure that loyal, repeat customers can't use the old bases to charge the new handsets. Keeping the base design the same would reward loyalty, but instead Panasonic literally goes to special effort to make sure that repeat customers are screwed on this. For that reason alone, I'll go out of my way to avoid buying anything whatsoever from Panasonic in the future.

title: Flyover Nation- A window into our country's soul.
text:
I bought this book as a gift for my father, who has spent his entire adult life working in the industrial Midwest. It was a challenging subject, as his community often feels misunderstood or overlooked by coastal media narratives, but this book handles the topic with such profound empathy and journalistic integrity that it resonated deeply with him. The author does not offer easy answers or cheap political talking points. Instead, he takes the time to truly listen to the people living in the flyover states, capturing their fears, their dignity, and their complex relationship with modern America.

The narrative structure is compelling, weaving personal anecdotes with broader economic and cultural analysis without ever feeling academic or detached. I found myself reading late into the night, genuinely moved by the human stories at the center of the argument. It is rare to find a work that challenges you to think differently without being preachy. My father actually set it down multiple times to reflect on passages, which rarely happens with non-fiction. This is not just a book about politics; it is a testament to the resilience of the American spirit. It has sparked meaningful conversations at our dinner table about topics we usually avoid. If you are looking for a nuanced, heart-wrenching, and ultimately hopeful look at what makes this country tick, this is essential reading. It deserves every star and more for its courage and clarity.

title: Decent product, good price, functions as advertised
text:
tl;dr version: For $32 you can't go wrong.

I've been using this backpack cooler almost daily since I bought it two weeks ago. I use three, small rectangular "blue ice" packs placed on the bottom, on top of a small, folded dish towel to absorb any condensation. I haven't used it with ice. Some reviewers say the top zipper leaks if you use ice that melts. I can well imagine...so don't use ice.

There is plenty of room in this thing for enough food and drinks for two or three people. It's kept me fed through a few double shifts and everything stays cold for a good 20 hours. The blue ice packs are still half-frozen after that long. I live in a temperate part of the country, I can't say anyone in Arizona or Nevada, for instance, would have the same results, so caveat emptor.

The straps are long and wide enough to be comfortable when wearing this as a backpack, and I'm a pretty big guy. It also carries well slung over one shoulder, which is not always the case.

Some of the reviews fault the zippers for breaking. Yeah, I can see that happening if you jerk them, are impatient, or in a hurry and not paying attention. I've had no problems with them. Same with the stitching; I pack out at about 20 pounds and I've seen no signs of wear and tear, yet. It has only been two weeks, sure, but still...

Pros: keeps food plenty cold for a whole day when used with re-freezable ice packs; lots of room inside, comfortable straps. Netting pockets for water bottles, etc. on the sides are deep and big enough for wide bottles.

Cons: zippered storage compartments on the front and top are inadequate. No "waterproof" storage compartment for keys, phone, etc.

title: Audience
text:
I finished reading Supreme Court Justice Stephen Breyer’s book titled, The Authority of the Court and the Peril of Politics, thinking about his intended audience. If his audience is the informed American citizen, his claims of the court not being political come across as naïve. If his audience is his fellow justices and his message is for them not to overreach because they may find the authority of the court diminished, that made a bit more sense to me. I thought of Alan Greenspan’s confession about his foundational error in the runup to the financial crisis. He assumed that banks would act prudently as a form of self-preservation. As we know, they didn’t. Why Breyer might expect fellow justices to preserve the authority of the Supreme Court by not overreaching in their decisions, I can’t imagine. We will all watch the exercise of power and learn how much peril can be absorbed by our democratic republic.

I have read a couple of Karen Robards books before and was anxious to read this one. I did not regret it!! She has an independent and feisty heroine in Madeline (Maddie) Fitzgerald, a determined and sexy hero in Sam McCabe and lots of fun secondary characters such as E.P. Wynee, Sam's partner; Cynthia Gardner, also on Sam's team and Jon and Susan. The dog, Zelda, is also a riot.

McCabe is an FBI special agent tracking a serial killer who calls him to leave clues. Maddie is the proud owner of a small advertising agency that is due to make a presentation the next morning at a dog food manufacturing company in New Orleans. Maddie is attacked and nearly killed in her hotel room. The killer also kills another Madeline Fitzgerald who is staying at the same hotel that same night/early morning. Maddie has secrets in her past that make her distrust law enforcement in general and the FBI in particular so lots of fireworks when McCabe & Wynne track her down to question her. Maddie & Jon make their presentation and win business with the dog food company by suggesting the owner's dog to appear in the ads and on a new logo.

Maddie & Jon fly back to St. Louis but Maddie is afraid her past is catching up with her. In the meantime, McCabe is convinced the killer will go after her again as she is the one who got away. Lots of close calls, comic relief from Zelda (the dog) and Wynne, romance and plots twists follow.

The case consists of two pieces: the tight skin with a clip that goes directly on the iPod (and covers all but the screen and headphone input and port), and the hard case that hugs the front of the skin/iPod and covers the screen.

The clip:
-It has no spring, so I am not sure how long it will last without snapping.
-It seems that you can not separate the clip from the skin without damaging at least one of them.
-It only has 180 degrees of rotation, so you can't turn it upside down (I prefer one that has 360 degrees, but for most this is probably not an issue)
-It does not rotate easily. If you wear pants that are made with light material, when you attempt to rotate it, you will end up just twisting your pants. But for those that prefer it not to move around, this is a good thing.

The case:
For the most part it fits the iPod quite well. The only exception is the hole for the "hold" switch does not line up. Turning "hold" off is not a problem. Switching it on, though, takes a little bit of effort sometimes (emphasis on "little").

This also comes with a a lanyard attached to a plug that fits into the port. This can be used instead of/as a backup to the clip.

All in all it is a good product, and I would definitely recommend it.

title: teenage mutant ninja turtles shellraiser
text:
I have been a massive fan of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles since I was a kid in the nineties, so when I saw the Shellraiser on sale, I knew I had to grab it for my seven-year-old nephew. He is currently in his absolute TMNT phase, and this toy has become his favorite thing in his entire room. It has been over three weeks, and it is still in remarkably good condition despite being dragged around the house, taken on "missions" in the backyard, and occasionally stepped on. The build quality is surprisingly robust for a toy in this price range. The treads grip well on both carpet and hardwood, which means it actually moves where you want it to go rather than getting stuck under the sofa legs every two seconds.

The sound effects are a nice touch without being overwhelmingly loud or annoying to adults. It plays the classic theme song and has a few explosion noises that really sell the immersive experience for the kids. The remote control is intuitive enough for a child to use independently after just a few minutes of practice, which was a huge bonus. I also appreciate that the opening mechanism for the rear cargo area works smoothly; it allows easy access to the four original action figures, which fits snugly inside. We did have to buy new batteries immediately, as the included ones were likely just for display, but that is standard practice. Assembly was minimal—just snapping on the treads and putting batteries in the shell. It is a fantastic gift option that offers genuine play value rather than just being a static display piece. If you are looking for a durable, engaging toy that brings the nostalgia of the cartoon to life, the Shellraiser is worth every penny. My nephew’s joy when he opened it was priceless, and that alone makes the purchase a success. Highly recommended for any young ninja turtle fan.

title: Great but not for me
text:
The writing in James Baldwin's 1953 Go Tell It on the Mountain is as good as writing gets, but this book wasn't for me. It's told through the filter of the Christian religion and while that may hold much sociological interest to many, none of it was new to me, though it is fascinating to think about it: A Middle Eastern religion, transformed in Europe, exported from there to America and then forced on unwilling slaves from Africa. But growing up in a fairly diverse East Coast city and having been raised going to church until I was no longer required to, the religious aspects of this book didn't interest me. The only part of it I found compelling was Part Three in which that element was least present, which the section that described the main character's origin story.
 If you're interested and don't know a lot about the influence of the church on American Blacks, this book—its working title was "Crying Holy"—is for you. Otherwise, you might be more interested in Baldwin's other works.

 On a bright, summer day, bright in her memory forever, she came into the store alone, wearing her best white summer dress and with her hair, newly straightened and curled at the ends, tied with a scarlet ribbon. She was going to a great church picnic with her aunt, and had come in to buy some lemons. She passed the owner of the store, who was a very fat man, sitting out on the sidewalk, fanning himself; he asked her, as she passed, if it was hot enough for her, and she said something and walked into the dark, heavy-smelling store, where flies buzzed and where Richard sat on the counter reading a book.
 She felt immediately guilty about having disturbed him, and muttered apologetically that she only wanted to buy some lemons. She expected him to get them for her in his sullen fashion and go back to his book, but he smiled and said:
 "Is that all you want? You better think now. You sure you ain't forgot nothing?"

title: The plight of the Third World
text:
Accomplished master of the police procedural Henning Mankell strays from this genre in his latest novel, "Kennedy's Brain". In his novel, Mankell in the guise of a mystery, has penned what is in reality a social commentary. Mankell who resides at least partially in Mozambique, takes aim at the plight of the African underprivileged particularly relating to the AIDS epidemic and it's exploitation by the pharmaceutical companies.

Swedish archaeologist Louise Cantor whose specialty is ancient Greek artifracts is leading an expedition in Greece sponsored by Uppsala university. She happily anticipates taking a break to return to Stockholm and visit her son Henrik. Much to her shock and dismay she arrives at his flat, unable to raise him on the phone, to find him lying dead in bed. She is stunned to learn that an autopsy confirms that he overdosed on barbiturates.

Unable to believe that Henrik would take his own life she commences her own investigation. She travels across the world to a remote area of Australia to recruit her estranged husband Aron and inform him of their son's death. Together they go through his papers that direct them to an apartment their son kept in Barcelona. Hacking into his computer they discover that he was HIV positive and that he had business that took him to Mozambique.

Louise Cantor proceeds to Africa after the mysterious disappearance of her ex husband. While there she is confronted by danger and the horrors of a village designed to care for AIDS victims where Henrik had worked. She discovers that there is quite a bit more going on there than administering to the sick.

Mankell paints a graphic picture of the misery endured by the suffering in Africa while being critical of those who opportunistically use them for financial gain. The plot of "Kennedy's Brain", metaphor for an inexplicable and secretive mystery is very much similar to Le Carre's "The Constant Gardener".

title: Excellent account of the "Emergency"
text:
I served in the army in Malaya in 1957-58, and found this book to be an excellent "refresher course" when writing my own stories for my family; we have long-standing connections with Malaya, from before WWII until just after Merdeka, and I was able to fill in some gaps and correct some errors.

I've deducted one star because of two problems: first, it is in serious need of an index, and second, there isn't much coverage of the later stages just before Merdeka (August 1957) - perhaps the CTs were effectively beaten by then, but we felt (perhaps mistakenly) that Malaya was still definitely a war zone. I suppose that when you are in the jungle and your rations are being parachuted in you get a distorted view of history!

This book dates from 1971, so naturally does not have some of the information that later writers have been able to find as records are released. I recommend Margaret Shennan's biography of John Davis, "Our Man in Malaya" (2007), as an excellent addition to the field. But of course F. Spencer Chapman's classic, "The Jungle is Neutral", is required reading for anyone trying to understand what jungle warfare really feels like.

title: Seems to be a good product.
text:
I have been searching for a reliable solution for my golden retriever, Buster, for quite some time now, and I must admit, I approached this purchase with a mix of high hopes and significant skepticism. My dog has always been prone to chewing on things he shouldn't, particularly during his teething phase and when he is left alone for extended periods. The product description promised durability, mental stimulation, and hours of engaging playtime, which sounded too good to be true. After using it for about three weeks, I feel compelled to share my honest experience to help other pet owners make an informed decision.

First, let’s address the build quality. On one hand, the material feels sturdy and the design is intuitive enough for a dog to understand quickly. Buster picked it up in less than five minutes, which was impressive. He spends a good amount of time trying to get the treats out, and that alone has kept him occupied while I work from home. The Kong-like shape is effective for freezing treats, which adds an extra layer of engagement during hot summer days. From a utility standpoint, it does exactly what it claims to do regarding keeping a pet busy and distracted from household furniture.

However, there are notable downsides that prevent this product from earning a five-star rating in my book. The main issue is the cleanup process, which is unnecessarily complicated. It has many small crevices and seams where food particles get trapped. No matter how much I scrub it with hot soapy water, I still worry about bacteria buildup or that strange smell that sometimes lingers after washing. This is a significant drawback for a product that is supposed to be a daily staple in your home. Additionally, while Buster loves it, he has managed to crack a small section after a particularly aggressive play session, despite the claims of being "indestructible." He never internalizes, seldom jumps to conclusions, and just proceeds along the rightness of his course without question. He is a Faulknerian character distilled down to the basics, so unsophisticated he is hilariously honest.

Norwood is a fast-paced comedy of the simpleton winning out in the end because his sights are so low he can't lose, and Charles Portis' social commentary should not be missed, but if you do, the dialogue alone is worth the read. And if the characters in Norwood seem too silly to be real? Well, I recognized them more than I care to admit.

text:
I rarely write reviews, but Filled My Soul moved me enough that I had to share. I bought this book during a time when life felt noisier and more hurried than I wanted, and it turned out to be exactly what I didn’t know I was looking for.

The writing is intimate without being indulgent; the author speaks with a warmth that feels like a conversation with a wise friend. Each chapter offered small, practical reflections that were easy to read but lingered long after I closed the book. I found myself pausing to journal, to try a suggested practice, or simply to sit in quiet appreciation. Those simple exercises slowly added up to a noticeable shift in how I approached my days.

What I appreciated most was the balance between insight and accessibility. This isn’t preachy self-help jargon — it’s grounded, humble guidance that respects where you are while gently nudging you toward more meaning and presence. The anecdotes felt real, not staged, and the author’s humility made the lessons feel attainable.

The book’s pacing was perfect; I could read a chapter in one sitting or savor it over several days. The physical copy I received was well-produced, with pleasant typography and a durable cover.

If you’re looking for a book that offers gentle clarity and practical tools for cultivating a deeper, calmer life, Filled My Soul is a lovely companion. I’ll be returning to passages again and recommending it to friends.

title: Great tent - try not to set it up alone.....
text:
I bought this tent for a weekend family camping trip and overall it exceeded my expectations — sturdy, roomy, and well thought out. We’re a family of four (two adults, two kids) and the tent comfortably fit two queen air mattresses plus gear along the perimeter with room to sit. The fabric feels durable and the seams look well sealed; after a night of heavy rain nothing leaked and the ground stayed dry. Ventilation is excellent — the mesh windows and ceiling kept the inside from getting stuffy even in the afternoon heat, and the guy lines and stakes held firm when the wind picked up.

My only serious caveat, and the reason for the title of this review, is setup. Instructions are adequate but the poles and clips require an extra set of hands. I tried to wrestle it up solo and made it more stressful and slower than necessary — there were a few moments where I wished for a partner to help hold corners while I threaded poles. With two people the setup took under 15 minutes. Takeaway: don’t plan to put it up alone if you want a quick, frustration-free start to your outing.

Small touches I appreciated: the vestibule for muddy boots, interior pockets for lights/phones, and the heavy-duty zippers that felt solid. The packed size is reasonable for car camping. If you need a reliable family tent and can have at least two people for setup, this is a great purchase. Highly recommend.

title: Fits my Mosin Nagant 91/30
text:
I bought this sling hoping it would be an affordable, authentic-feeling replacement for the tired, cracked leather piece on my Mosin Nagant 91/30, and it exceeded my expectations. Right out of the package the quality was obvious — the leather has a nice, solid feel without being overly stiff, and the stitching looks durable and well-done. Installation was straightforward; the hardware lined up with the rifle’s original fittings and I had it mounted and adjusted in less than ten minutes.

Fit is excellent. The length and buckle placement are right where they should be for the Mosin Nagant 91/30, allowing me to carry the rifle comfortably for extended periods and to bring it to the shoulder quickly without fumbling. The sling holds the rifle securely when slung and doesn’t slip under load. The leather softened a bit with rubbing-in and now conforms to my body nicely.

Functionally it performs exactly as advertised — a dependable field sling that feels period-appropriate. Aesthetically it complements the rifle well; the color and finish match the vintage look of my Mosin. After a couple of range sessions and a few walks in the woods, there’s only mild, attractive patina developing.

If I have one nitpick it’s that the edge finish could be slightly smoother, but that’s purely cosmetic and hasn’t affected performance. Overall I’m very pleased — great value for the price and a perfect fit for the 91/30. If you’re looking for a solid replacement sling that’s ready to use out of the box, this one is a great choice. Five stars.

title: Squeakiest chair ever
text:
I wanted to like this chair — I bought it for camping and tailgating because the photos made it look sturdy, compact, and comfortable. In practice it’s a mixed bag, and I’m giving it two stars because of one major issue that ruins most of the experience: it is the squeakiest chair I have ever owned.

Right out of the box the frame seemed solid and the fabric felt ok for the price. Setup was straightforward and the chair folded down to a nice compact carry size. It is reasonably light and the included carry bag is handy, which is why I still use it occasionally despite the problem.

But when you sit down and shift even slightly, the metal frame lets out a loud, high-pitched squeak. Moving from standing to seated is like a chorus of tiny brakes. At a quiet campsite or during a game, the noise is embarrassing and constant. I tried tightening all the screws, applying lubricant to the joints, and even layering some cloth at the contact points — nothing fully fixed it. The squeak is present whether the chair is placed on grass, gravel, or concrete.

Comfort-wise, the seat is average for a folding chair. The back offers minimal support and after a couple hours you start to feel it. The cup holder is useful but flimsy. Weight capacity seems fine for my needs, and the fabric has held up after a few uses.

If you only need an inexpensive portable chair and can tolerate (or fix) the noise, it serves a purpose. But if you want quiet, comfortable seating for longer outdoor events, look elsewhere. text:
OK, first the things I liked about the Littlest Pet Shop. All the parts were easy to assemble with clear instructions. The front panel is hinged so that little hands could get into the shop. Three "littlest pets" were included with the set. (It irks me when these "branded" sets are sold without the action figures.)

Now, for the things I didn't like. Though the sides, front, and base are made of sturdy plastic, the back panel was very thin cardboard. I had four little girls ages 5 to 10 "helping" me assemble the set, although they did more playing than assembling. Before we had gotten all the Deco bits taken off the plastic frames, the back panel had popped out of the frame. To restore it properly, several pieces had to be taken apart. For a play set that retails for $40, seems to me that the back panel could have been made from plastic, too. The sales counter was also a problem. It came in two pieces: the top and the base. The only way I could get the counter top to stay fastened to the base was to attach it with double-sided tape.

The set contains 135 pieces. A few pieces are decals. There are maybe 20 larger pieces. However, the rest are very small plastic pieces, the kind that small pets and toddlers choke on. The kind that children leave all over the floor and you step on in the middle of the night on your way to the bathroom or refrigerator. The kind you're still digging out from beneath the car seat when the child graduates from high school. Enough said?

In spite of my lack of enthusiasm for the Littlest Pets Shop Style Set, the 4 girls loved it. They happily played with everything. They set up the shop, decorated the side walls, the dog house, and the pets with the Deco Bits. They let the monkey swing from the chandelier and gave the pets new names. They just had fun. On their way out the door, the two older girls were asking their mom if they could go to the store. No one had to asked why...

title: Sarah has a beautiful way with words
text:
The 411 by Maria:
I received this book right before Mother's Day. It is absolutely incredible. It is one perfect, powerful poem. A poem made into a book for mother's to give daughters and friends to give each other.

Having a daughter for me, was on my bucket list. I knew I didn't have much say in the matter and prayed for Goddess as hard as I could without going overboard afraid that if I begged too hard, God would feel it was unfair and unwarranted.

What Sarah Kay does is takes everything I have ever felt or thought about my daughter and put it into words. Every girl should have a copy of this book. They should read it and re-read it because Sarah speaks the truth. Life will hit you in the face and wait for you to get back up so it can kick you in the stomach. This is a healthy dose of reality but written in a poetic, joyful way, truly beautiful way.

Apologize when you've done something wrong. .
But don't you ever apologize for the way your eyes refuse
to stop shining; your voice is small,
But don't you ever stop singing.

That lines brings tears to my eyes. It is everything I would have wanted someone to say to me as a child and it exactly how I want my Goddess to grow up. Never ever stop singing.

After you read the book for the 10th time, go back and watch Sarah Kay read it. She really is very special and I want to thank her for writing everything I would want to say if I knew how.

title: Alamo Questions
text:
Chariton explores a number of questions revolving around the tragedy of Alamo. Most of the questions he explores are, in fact, not legends but legitimate questions as to what did or did not happen in an around the time that the Alamo was attacked and the defenders slaughtered. Generally I agree with Chariton's deductions although I also believe that all testimony regarding the Zuber must regarded with extreme suspicion. Zuber claimed that he got his information from Louis Rose, the supposed only deserter from Alamo. In a manner resembling Thucidides, Zuber admitted embellishing [making up] Travis' final speech to the troops, including the famous 'line in the sand'. In my opinion, if Zuber lied about anything, then it should be rightfully assumed that he lied about everything.

I think Zuber's testimony is an insult to all the men who died at Alamo. Their heroism stands by itself and required no second hand editorialism. I'll go even further than that to proclaim my own belief that Louis Rose--if he ever existed--never testified to Zuber. Zuber made up the entire story 'whole-cloth'.

Ron

title: Needs a lot of drying time
text:
I wanted to like this product — the packaging looked nice and the shade matched what I expected from the photos. I'm giving it three stars because it has both positives and drawbacks that are worth knowing before you buy.

First the good: the formula goes on smoothly and provides decent coverage once it's fully dry. It doesn't have a strong chemical smell, and I didn't experience any irritation on my skin. After it set, my makeup looked fairly natural and the finish was pleasant — not overly matte or greasy. It also lasted a reasonable part of the day without needing constant touch-ups.

Now the big caveat: the drying time. It takes much longer to fully set than I anticipated. I followed the instructions, and while the product felt tacky for a long time, it didn't truly dry for nearly twice as long as similar items I’ve used. That meant I had to be extra careful getting dressed, putting on jewelry, or touching my hair. A few times it transferred onto my scarf and sleeve despite trying to be careful. If you’re in a hurry most mornings, this will be frustrating.

Another small issue is that if you try to layer it before it’s fully dry, it pills and becomes uneven. I learned to apply a thinner layer and wait patiently, but that reduced the coverage and required a second coat with more drying time.

Overall, it’s an okay product if you plan ahead and don’t need something quick. Good finish and tolerable wear, but the long drying time and transfer risk keep it from being a favorite. I’d recommend it only to people who can spare the extra time for application.

title: It is like having a conversation with her
text:
Full disclosure: I have met Angelo Lowery at a writer’s retreat in Sedona Arizona. Angelo is in person, as she is portrayed in her memoir, “I am and the Spirit Walks with me,” a force to be reckoned with.
When I met Angelo, it was the first time in my life I met someone who has a direct line of communication to God. Her eyes are full of light, and she exudes a natural sense of strength and power. Reading her book, it was a surprise to me to hear all that she has endured in her life – abuse, betrayal, stunning loss. And yet, in her life, she has been able to rise above the pain to directly touch God. She has turned betrayal into blessing, loss into communion and pain into healing.
Angelo’s book is imperfect, as are many self-published books that do not have the benefit of a high-rolling publishing house behind them. But in its imperfection, it is perfectly Angelo. It is like having a conversation with her. She writes as she speaks, in a lovely, sometimes innocent, sometimes all-knowing, inspired and warm tone….until she speaks the words she hears from God. It was fascinating to read how distinctly different were the voices of her book – hers versus God’s.
Angelo is a warrior, she has survived countless horrors that would crumple the best of us. How did she do that? She shares that she always knew she was somehow chosen by God to do special work (Angelo is a gifted healer today). Was this the key to her resilience? For many who suffer adversity, their experience becomes an excuse to visit adversity on others. For Angelo, it became an opportunity to draw close to God and heal both herself and others.
I would love for Angelo to share next how we mere mortals, those of us who have not felt chosen, can also rise above adversity in our lives to become a conduit of good and love and spirit as she has done. Thank you for sharing your heroin’s journey, Angelo.

2) Make sure to align the dot on the bean holder as described in the manual.
3) Be sure the bean holder is all the way seated before turning it to engage.
4) Turn it slowly to make sure it's seated and engaging correctly.

text:
22 Nov 2020

At $45.00, this USB-C magnetic adapter is much more expensive than the less expensive $17.00 to $22.00 magnetic adapters. I have not tried the cheaper adapters mainly because this adapter has 24 pins, and the cheaper adapters have a max of 20 pins.

I am using this magnetic adapter on a 2019 16" MBP. As you can see from the picture, the computer is charging at 94W (using 96W power supply) which is the same charge wattage as when the USB-C cable is connected directly to the computer USB-C port. So the limitation is with the power supply itself not delivering the full 96W, and not an issue with this magnetic adapter.

I understand that there are concerns about this bulky adapter physically interfering with adjacent USB-C ports, but at least with this computer, I can connect this magnetic adapter in one computer port and another USB-C cable in the adjacent USB-C port with about 1mm clearance (see pic).

title: "original work of art" a tad too generous
text: When a book is released around the time of an author's death the literary world seems to shower him/her with an insane amount of praise that one has to wonder if death didn't come calling would would this book be so highly praised.  This is a short book (only about 244 pages which is slightly misleading because of page margins and text size this book is much shorter).  It's plot is compelling and it is wonderfully descriptive.  I found  Matthiessen' s tendency to switch between writing from the point of view of the main character to casual observer confusing and wish he would have stuck to one or the other.  The main character's purpose for being in this place and time (when you finally learn why)  is a great and equally tragic story line and by itself is enough to carry the reader.  The introduction of all minor characters just dilutes the story and introduces a bunch of characters that we don't care about and have absolutely no reason to care about.  Overall I gave this book 3 stars simply because the cast of characters and their relationship to the story is unmoving and distracting from the good aspects of this book.  It would be silly to tell someone not to read this book because the reality is, this is such a short book that even if you hated it you're not investing a huge chunk of your time.  It's not like reading a 1,000 page epic like PILLARS OF THE EARTH where if you hate it or get bored you've still got hundreds of pages to get through before you can properly decide what you're overall opinion is.

title: When Simple Faith is Simply Not Enough
text:
"Today, twenty-first century theology tends to make religion a belief based upon faith rather than a belief of faith based upon fact. History, science, and conflicting Scriptures are all too often dismissed when they conflict with accepted creeds or dogma. Most Judeo-Christians are taught there are certain areas of their religion they should not question, causing the phrase “it is a matter of faith” to be well-worn and overused.
Scripture encourages individuals to question their idea of God."
And question it she did!
For Jodell Onstott, like so many of us, simple faith was simply not enough. Unable to dismiss the passionate; yet, conflicting views of countless denominations… the seemingly endless interpretations of a single text… the bearing of historic facts and archeological discoveries… the consequence of scientific evidences… Jodell embarked upon a decade long mission to discover the not so simple truth. And though the title of the subsequent book, “YHVH Exists” may eliminate the suspense of her ultimate conclusion, Jodell’s journey is a masterpiece of well-organized testimonies and closely examined proofs. Leaving no stone unturned, her systematic examination of the data demonstrates a sincere desire to reach an objective opinion.
The long-awaited “YHVH Exists” is a thorough and fascinating study that will challenge your most hidden preconceptions, and, may well find itself on the more than one bestseller’s list in the process.
Well worth the wait!

title: Great product ! Great for my long trip from VA to VT !
text: I purchased this for a long trip from VA to VT. I wanted to talk on the phone if needed, and do it hands free. This works great, as I had no Bluetooth in my 08 Nissan Altima. It only works through your car speakers when you have the radio on AUX input. This wasn't a problem on a long trip, as I had thousands of songs on my Samsung Galaxy S5 to listen to. I could listen to my music, skip songs when I wanted by pushing a button, and when a call came in all I had to do was say "answer" or push a button to accept the call. When the call ends, the music picks back up where it left off. To make a call, I could do it by voice (call Tina at home) or use the phone to dial it manually. It then stops the music and dials who you are calling. It doesn't work unless you have your car radio on AUX. You can't use the actual radio and use the SoundBot at the same time. It comes with a 12v plug (cigarette lighter plug) that has 3 USB outlets on it. One of those is used for the SoundBot, the other 2 can be used for GPS, phone charger, etc. Then there is a 3.5mm plug that goes to the AUX input on your radio. Your phone then connects wirelessly through Bluetooth to the SoundBot. I used my GPS on my phone, and the directions was heard through my car speakers over my music I was playing through my phone. I made and received many calls on my trip, and everybody said they heard me loud and clear. Great price on the SoundBot, and I loved it. I can't use it when listening to my local radio stations at home, but if I have it plugged in and connected, I can push the AUX button on my radio and use it then to talk. Or push AUX then make a call if I need to. A great product that works as intended. I love it !

title: Perfect OEM Replacement (+ install instructions) for Parkside TR-14FT-COMBO
text:
Parkside TR-14FT-COMBO
100% OE Replacement

If this is your trampoline, this mat is a perfect replacement for the original in thickness, stitching and quality of nylon tabs and galvanized rings. The only difference is the branding printed on the center and a vinyl cover over the stitching to protect from UV (better than the original being replaced from 2008).

You WILL need a spring tool and at least a second set of hands to install (or at least hand you springs). And the mat will seem too small at first.

TO INSTALL:
(read through all steps before starting)

NOTE 1: Counting mat rings / frame holes accurately is essential. Get off by 1 and you have to start over.

NOTE 2: Be careful to pull springs straight out (and keep an eye on it as you're pulling) from the mat ring to the frame hole so that the spring stays hooked in the point of the ring. Do not allow the spring to slip to one of the sides or a cascade of problems will ensue.

1) Select a ring on the mat and attach a spring to it and to the trampoline frame

2) Count 42 rings around on the mat and attach another spring

3) Count 42 holes around on the frame and attach the other end of that spring

4) Count 21 rings from either spring and add the next spring; do the same for holes and attach

5) Repeat step 4 on the opposite side

(You now have 4 springs attached at each of the 90º points, creating 4 quadrants)

6) In your first quadrant, count 10 rings and holes from a spring and attach another

7) In the quadrant directly across from your first, count 10 rings and holes and attach another

8) Repeat for the other 2 quadrants

9) Now start filling in the gaps, alternating to the opposite side every couple of springs. The idea is to keep alternating sides so that the tension remains as even as is possible.

***It might seem easier to just start working your way around, but the pull will become uneven, increasing the likelihood of having a ring slip.***

Feel free to message me for any further info.

title: More like "Helping Badger Overcome Depression"
text: I was surprised to see this book so breezily reviewed.  I myself found it disturbing.  There are lots of good books around that deal with bad moods--"Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Really Bad  Day" and "Today I Feel Silly & Other Moods That Make My  Day" come to mind.  This book goes way beyond moodiness and knocks on  the door of clinical depression.  First, the animals find Badger sitting in  his chair in the dark.  When they switch on the light, Badger snaps at them  to turn it off and leave him be.  The other animals leave, but Mole is  worried about Badger so he stays and cleans up the place a bit. Badger  eventually speaks: "I'm sorry about this. 'Spect I'll get over it.  But right now, I'm just no good, you know.  No good for anything."  Mole tells him they'll "just wait".  Eventually the animals call  a doctor.  Badger refuses to see her and sends Mole out to get rid of her  and the other animals trying to help:  "Close the curtains," he  begged Mole.  "Keep them away."  Then we have a scene where Mole  watches Badger "staring and dozing and turning heavily in his  chair."  YIKES! And then, just when you're sure Mole is going to be  calling the suicide hotline, things turn rosy and child-appropriate again.  Mole comes up with the idea of an Awards Ceremony (this causes Badger's  eyes to move "sharply for the first time in days").  Badger and  all the other animals attend.  Badger wins all sorts of awards for being a  good person/badger.  At last he feels "appreciated" and is happy.  Everyone dances.  I was confused (and creeped out).  My child was  confused:  "How come he wants to sit in the dark?...How come he  doesn't want the doctor to help him?...Doesn't he like the other animals  anymore?...Does he like them better now that they had a party for  him?"  If this had been a book to help children understand  depression--a book with an appropriate resolution and ending--it would have  been fine.  If this had been a book about a badger who was feeling glum and  unappreciated, who was then cheered up by an awards ceremony, it would have  been fine.  But this book is a bizarre marriage of the two and it is AWFUL.

title: Noise Reduction Techniques
text:
There is a specific topic in this book that I have not seem covered in any of the 25+ book that I have on electromagnetic phenomena. The topic is the shield cut-off frequency of a coaxial cable. Common-mode currents at low frequencies (below a few hundred hertz) cause noise problems with coaxial cables, but signals above tens of kilohertz do not. This is vital data which is apparently not explained in many text books. For me, this topic justifies the cost of the text. Having said that, I am annoyed because the book is quite expensive relative to other books of its size and age. The point is that you have to buy it, but it is expensive to do so.
Even an advanced designer will benefit from this book, although you, like me, won't necessarily want to read all of it. It is sufficient to pick and choose areas of particular interest. The less advanced designer would clearly benefit more and the book would therefore represent better value for them. Given a choice between this one and Morrison's Grounding and Shielding Techniques in Instrumentation, pick this one. This one is more technically accurate and useful.

text:
I bought this product because the packaging and reviews promised a gentle, effective addition to my skincare routine, but my experience ended up being a mixed bag. First, the positives: the scent is pleasant without being overpowering, and the texture feels nice going on—light and non-greasy. After a few weeks of use I did notice a slight improvement in overall skin smoothness, and it didn’t strip my skin the way some stronger formulas do.

That said, there are a few disappointments. The results were subtler than I expected from the marketing. I was hoping for more noticeable brightening and reduction in uneven tone, but those changes have been minimal. Also, the pump on my bottle started to stick after about three weeks, which made dispensing messy and frustrating. For the price point I expected better quality control.

I also had a small breakout after introducing the product, although it’s hard to say whether that was caused by this alone since I had a few other variables in my routine. I stopped using it for a week and the irritation subsided; when I reintroduced it slowly, the reaction did not recur, so it may be sensitivity rather than a full incompatibility.

Overall, I think this might work well for someone looking for a gentle, light formula and who doesn’t need dramatic results. It’s not a bad product, but it’s not a miracle worker either, and the packaging durability issues left me underwhelmed. I’m giving it three stars because it’s fine, just not worth repurchasing for me.

title: Worst air mattress
text:
I never write negative reviews because I prefer to give people the benefit of the doubt, but this air mattress is absolutely the worst purchase I have made in the last five years. I bought it specifically for a weekend camping trip with my family, thinking it would be a convenient alternative to inflating and deflating sleeping bags every single night. That was a massive mistake. I followed the instructions exactly, using the recommended pump to inflate it to the maximum pressure level indicated in the manual. For the first thirty minutes, it seemed firm enough. I felt confident. However, by the time I actually got into bed, I could already feel a significant loss of support. It did not take long at all for the bottom side to begin drooping, creating a hammock effect that was incredibly uncomfortable and bad for my back.

By the second hour of sleep, I had to wake up multiple times because the mattress was slowly deflating on its own. I checked every seam and valve to ensure it was closed tightly, but there was no leak anywhere. It was just the material itself expanding and failing to hold the air pressure properly. The construction feels incredibly flimsy and cheap. The surface texture is rough and provides almost no grip, so I kept sliding off to one side throughout the entire night. It was a cold, hard, lumpy nightmare. I tried using the electric pump again in the morning to re-inflate it, but it barely went up. I am genuinely shocked that this product is still on the market with such a low rating that hasn't deterred buyers. Do not waste your money on this garbage. If you need an air mattress, save your time and go buy a reputable brand from a well-known manufacturer. This item is essentially trash wrapped in plastic. I threw it in the recycling bin immediately after this trip. It is an insult to customers who pay full price for comfort and reliability. I am extremely disappointed and will never trust this brand again.

title: The Power of Now, Is Taking Control of Your Emotions!
text:
I bought this book after feeling completely overwhelmed by the stresses of my daily life and a constant cycle of anxiety about the future. For years, I felt like my emotions were driving me rather than the other way around. After reading The Power of Now, I can honestly say my perspective on mental health and mindfulness has completely shifted.

The core message of the book is simple yet profound: the only moment that truly exists is the present. While that sounds basic, the way the author explains how to detach from the ego and stop the internal noise is life-changing. I found the practical exercises incredibly helpful. Instead of getting swept away by a wave of anger or sadness, I now have a toolkit to observe those emotions without becoming them. It has given me a sense of peace that I didn't think was possible.

What I appreciate most is that it doesn't just tell you to stop worrying; it teaches you the mechanics of why we worry and how to break that loop. My relationships have improved because I am more present during conversations and less reactive during conflicts. I feel more centered, focused, and in control of my internal state than ever before.

If you feel like you are a slave to your moods or constantly living in your head, please give this book a chance. It is not a quick fix, but a deep dive into how to actually live your life. It is easily one of the most influential books I have ever read. Highly recommended for anyone seeking inner peace.

title: Afghanistan through the eyes of a child
text: A war-torn country plagued by violence.  An 11-year-old girl forced to risk her life and save her family. These are the realities in Deborah Ellis' novel "The Breadwinner" (Groundwood Books 2000).  Told from young Parvana's perspective, the story focuses on her family of six living in Kabul, Afghanistan.  After the Taliban take control of their city, Parvana's family is forced out of their large home by a bomb explosion and into a one-room apartment.  The women are removed from school and forced to stay in the house unless escorted by a male.  When Parvana's father is arrested because he attended university in England, their family must make the tough decision to have her pose as a boy in order to leave the house and work in the marketplace to earn money for food.  While working, Parvana runs into Shauzia, a girl she knew from school who is also posing as a boy to support her family. They start to work together and soon become close friends, encountering a number of sobering, scary situations along the way. Though children may not experience the same life, they will no doubt relate to Parvana's story and her arguments with her older sister, unfairness of chore responsibilities, and love for her family.  The Breadwinner is not a happy story with a happy conclusion, but one that will leave the reader with a different view of Afghanistan, as seen through the eyes of a child.  An author's note and glossary of terms serve as a helpful aide in introducing children to the history and culture of Afghanistan.

It keeps them physically active and completely entertained for long stretches of time. It is rare to find a toy that both children are equally obsessed with, but this has become the highlight of their day.

If you have toddlers or young children and you are looking for a way to keep them cool in the backyard without any stress, I highly recommend this. title: First impression and spooling line on the 2000 model.
text:
First impression:
- Body looks solid.
- if you can get it for about $20.00, you can't really complain, it's no $100 reel nor $200.00 but It will do the job.
- it's a good throw away, travel, back up reel at that price that can handle big fish. I would recommend spending more if you want something nicer but it would cost 2 or 3 times more.
-2000 spool size is too big. It's comparable to a 4000 spool. It's much deeper than a 2000. If I had to do it again I'll try for the 1000 instead for most applications.
- the line clip as shown on the picture fell off probably 3 times when messing with it at home or just spooling it. (I will probably try to glue the clip that holds it down together underneath before I end up losing it.) Highly recommend checking that all screw are tighten properly, you wouldn't want to loose any screw.
- the drag jumps from 33lb to no drag or 2/3lbs in about 10 clicks or a 90 degree dial turn. It's not very sensitive, it adjust at about 2/3lbs increments per clicks. You will probably need to set your drag gently to match your line if you do not want the line to snap under pressure for lighter lines. The drag is not ideal if you want to achieve a certain adjustable drag while fishing. Your drag might be too loose or too tight.
- line lay isn't impressive. It's ok at best just as shown. Not even. But it's only $20.00. When you fill pass 60%, it's hard not to get a few loose wrap. Tried to respool it couple times, I still have a few loose wrap every time. If you are picky and keep it under 60% you might be ok.

My guess is this reel will do the job for most applications and big fishes. The drag seems as if it will have very little to no play for some applications.

I will update after testing it enough on the water.

The colors are incredibly vivid and saturated, making every single page feel like a miniature piece of gallery art.

Whether it is the way the light hits the water or the tiny expressions on the characters' faces, the visual storytelling is just as powerful as the written text. The quality of the paper is also worth mentioning, as it is thick enough to prevent bleed-through and has a matte finish that makes the colors pop without creating a distracting glare.

It is rare to find a book where the images truly complement the narrative rather than just filling space. These illustrations add layers of emotion and atmosphere that the words alone could not convey. My niece was absolutely captivated by the imagery, and she keeps asking to read it again and again just so she can look at the pictures. 

Even for an adult, there is something deeply soothing and inspiring about the artistic style. It is clear that the illustrator put a tremendous amount of passion into this project. If you are looking for a book that will spark a child's imagination or if you simply appreciate high-quality artistic work, this is a must-have for your collection. It is a stunning addition to our bookshelf and one of the most visually appealing books I have ever owned. I highly recommend it to everyone.

title: Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and the three horsemen will do anything
text:
The final book of the Riders duology, and I’m happy with how it ended. Seeker by Veronica Rossi picks up where Riders left off. Sebastian has been trapped inside a dark dimension, and Darryn and the remaining three horsemen will do anything to bring him back.

One thing that I don’t care for about this book is the romance. Not every story needs a love story, especially a story that’s so tightly focused on a group of friends. The romance didn’t add to the story and Darryn’s continuous pulling away from Gideon was exasperating by the middle of the book.

Cutting the romance out of the story, like Riders, it’s a very neat story with a unique point of view. The remaining horsemen are doing all they can to find Bass in The Rift. The Rift forces them to face their fears, and face their innermost demons.

Without giving much away, the journey to find Sebastian is one full of haunting memories and really learning more about the characters. I don’t feel like there was as much character development as their was in the previous book, but I don’t think that it’s really a bad thing with this book. I also wish that this book only had Darryn’s or only Gideon’s point of view, like the first book, and not bouncing between both.

I do wish there were more books in the series. Books from the other horsemen’s points of views would be interesting, and I’d definitely read them. All in all, a series that is enjoyable and provides a pretty unique premise for the characters.

title: Diplomacy, work, humor, and adventure in this fine memoir
text:
This is Richard Williams' fascinating and wryly humorous account of two years as the U.S. Consul General in the Chinese city of Guangzhou (formerly called "Canton") from 1979 to 1981. His was the first American consulate to re-open in China after formal diplomatic relations with the PRC were established in 1979.

Readers interested in the development of U.S.-China relations will be fascinated -- and entertained -- by this book. Large strategic and foreign policy considerations moved China and the United States to establish relations. It was left to Foreign Service Officers such as Richard Williams and his team to make it all work -- first by setting up a new Foreign Service post, then by issuing visas, establishing commercial relations, traveling through China to report on local conditions, introducing the Big Mac, and escorting the first waves of American visitors.

Americans who know the more open China of the twenty-first century will, in this book, encounter the China making its first hesitant steps toward modernization and reform. The difficulties confronted by early official travelers, the lingering suspicion of America, the obfuscation of officials high and low, and the choices made by Foreign Service families before there were international schools are all described. Williams' wife Jane had left Tianjin as a girl; her reunions with family members in the PRC add poignant touches to the book.

This is a fine book for any young person thinking about a Foreign Service career. Although almost three decades have passed since Richard Williams and his family opened the post in Guangzhou, "At the Dawn of the New China" captures much of the enduring qualities of Foreign Service life.

The dartboard itself is also decent; the sisal is tight, the numbers are clear, and it feels like it will hold up to a lot of play over the next few years.

However, the darts included with the set are a complete disappointment. I understand that this is a budget-friendly bundle, but these darts are almost unusable. The tips are inconsistent, and the flights are made of a cheap plastic that curls or tears after just a few throws. More importantly, the balance is completely off. I found myself struggling to hit basic targets, not because of my skill, but because the darts wobble mid-air. They feel lightweight and cheap, almost like toys you would find in a carnival game rather than actual sporting equipment.

If you are buying this for a game room or a garage, be prepared to spend an extra twenty or thirty dollars immediately to buy a proper set of brass or tungsten darts. I ended up using an old set I had in the attic, and the difference in performance was night and day.

In short, the hardware is great, but the accessories are garbage. I am giving this three stars because the cabinet and board are high quality enough to justify the price, but the inclusion of such poor-quality darts is a major letdown. It is a good foundation for a home setup, but do not rely on the darts that come in the box. Buy the set for the board, and buy your darts elsewhere.

I picked up Should Be a Movie because the premise — a story so cinematic it feels like a screenplay waiting to happen — sounded irresistible, and for the most part the book delivers exactly that kind of experience. From the opening chapter I was immediately swept into lush, vividly described scenes that felt staged for a wide-screen adaptation: sweeping locations, sharp, witty dialogue, and a cast of characters who are equal parts charming and flawed.

The narrator’s voice is one of the book’s biggest strengths. There’s a self-aware, slightly sardonic tone that kept me smiling aloud on the subway and turning pages faster than I meant to. The protagonist is likable without being perfect; their internal monologue balances humor with genuine vulnerability, which made it easy to root for them even when their choices were messy. Secondary characters are well-drawn and memorable — a friend who steals every scene with deadpan one-liners, a love interest with complicated motives, and a rival who’s both infuriating and oddly relatable.

Pacing is generally strong. The middle section unspooled like a montage: set-ups, missteps, reconciliations, and a few surprises that kept me engaged. There are moments of quiet reflection that add emotional depth, and then the narrative will snap back into high-energy sequences that feel cinematic in the best way. The author’s knack for visual detail makes many scenes pop — I could see the city lights, hear the background music, and almost feel the weather on the characters’ skin.

That said, the book isn’t flawless. A couple of plot threads felt a bit underdeveloped, leaving me wanting more explanation about certain character motivations. And the ending, while satisfying, leans a little towards neatness; I would have enjoyed a touch more ambiguity or risk. A few sentences occasionally veered into purple prose, breaking the otherwise crisp rhythm, but those instances were infrequent.

Overall, Should Be a Movie is an entertaining, well-written read that will particularly delight anyone who loves contemporary fiction with strong dialogue and cinematic flair. It’s the kind of book you’ll want to recommend to friends and — yes — imagine being adapted for the screen. I’m giving it four stars because it’s consistently enjoyable and emotionally engaging, even if a little tightening in places would have made it exceptional.

title: Not for my cat!
text:
I purchased this chew toy expecting it to be a durable, long-lasting solution for my energetic tabby, but it turned out to be a complete waste of money. Within just twenty minutes of unboxing, my cat managed to shred the primary component into useless, floppy scraps. There was no tough, resilient resistance to speak of; it felt more like cheap, thin foam disguised as hard plastic.

Worse yet, the small pieces that detached posed a significant choking hazard. I found myself panicking, having to carefully scan the living room carpet for hours to ensure he hadn't ingested any of the broken bits. The scent was also overpowering and artificial, which actually made my cat lose interest in the toy entirely after the initial curiosity wore off. He preferred a crumpled paper ball from the recycling bin over this expensive, poorly designed product. For the price point, I expected much higher quality standards and safety assurances. It broke down too quickly, created a mess I didn't need, and failed to engage my pet in any meaningful way. I cannot recommend this to anyone who has a cat with even a moderate bite force. Save your money and buy a reputable brand that actually stands behind their durability claims. This was a disappointing experience from start to finish.

title: More then what I expected
text:
Writing this review a year into using this light on almost a daily bases.

This light is amazing and way more then I expected for it's small price tag.

I have used it both in pouring rain and in quite cold temperatures (around 5°F), and it has held up wonderfully. It has a few scraps on it from dropping it a few times, but I have noticed no reduced brightness or even battery life over its year of use.

The only problem I have had with it is it's mount. The little clip on the mount that holds the light in place recently snapped off. This has not been too much of an inconvenience for me as the light fits on snugly even without the clip and I easily jerry-rigged a rubber-band to provide some additional support in case i hit a large pothole on my bike.

The price for this light is pretty wonderful considering how well it has preformed over a year of use.

title: My first mommy calendar and i love it! Plenty of room to write on
text:
I just received my first mommy calendar in the mail, and I have to say, I absolutely love it! It exceeded all of my expectations, not just in terms of design, but in functionality. As a new mom, keeping track of my baby’s growth milestones, feeding schedules, and sleep patterns is crucial, but traditional journals often feel too cramped or complicated. This calendar strikes the perfect balance between simplicity and utility. The layout is intuitive, allowing me to quickly jot down daily notes without feeling overwhelmed by excessive fields or blank spaces that look intimidating.

What I appreciate most is the ample writing space provided on each day. Many calendars I’ve tried in the past have tiny text boxes that make handwriting a frustrating exercise in fine motor control. Here, there is plenty of room to write on the page. I can comfortably write down detailed observations about my little one’s day, from the color of his eyes to the sounds he makes, without running out of space. This has made the process of recording these fleeting moments much more enjoyable rather than a chore.

The paper quality is also impressive. It feels thick and durable, which means I don’t have to worry about ink bleeding through to the next page, a common issue with cheaper notebooks. This ensures that my records remain clean and legible for years to come, creating a lasting keepsake for my family. The binding is sturdy, allowing the calendar to lay flat on my nightstand or kitchen counter, which is incredibly convenient when I need to make a quick entry in the middle of the night or during a busy diaper change.

Beyond its practical features, the aesthetic appeal of the calendar brings a sense of joy to my daily routine. The soft, neutral tones are soothing to look at, and the overall design feels modern yet timeless. It doesn’t just sit there gathering dust; it becomes a cherished part of my daily life. I’ve already recommended it to several friends who have recently become parents, and I plan to buy another one as a gift for our upcoming baby shower. If you are looking for a meaningful way to document your journey into motherhood, I cannot recommend this product highly enough. It is a beautiful, functional, and heartfelt addition to any new parent’s home. I am so glad I made this purchase, and I know I will look back on these entries with immense fondness in the years to come. It truly is a wonderful tool for capturing the magic of these early days.

title: Will not fit regular kayak paddles
text:
I bought this paddle holder hoping it would keep my regular kayak paddles secure on the roof while transporting my boat. The idea and construction seemed solid in the photos, and I liked the price, so I gave it a try. After a few uses I have mixed feelings — mostly frustration.

First, the good: the materials feel reasonably sturdy for the price. The straps are thick and have robust buckles, and the foam cradle is dense enough that it didn’t collapse under the weight of the paddle. Installation on my roof rack was straightforward, and it didn’t shift around while driving once tightened. For small, slim paddles or very compact touring blades, I think this could work fine.

Now the big problem: it won’t fit standard kayak paddles. I have two common-size paddles (Suvine touring paddles, about 2.25" shaft diameter with modestly sized blades) and they simply don’t sit in the cradle the way the photos imply. The opening is too narrow and the foam forms around the shaft so tightly that you can’t get the paddles into position without bending them, which of course you should not do. I tried rotating and angling them, but they either won’t sit centered or the blades interfere with the straps. The product would work much better if the cradle opening were wider or if additional foam spacers were removable to accept larger shafts.

Customer support was polite when I contacted them, but their suggestion was to “force” the paddle in or swap to a different paddle size, which isn’t acceptable. For anyone with standard kayak paddles, I can’t recommend this unless you plan to modify it yourself (cutting foam out or replacing the cradle). Considering the decent build but critical sizing issue, two stars feels fair — it has potential but fails at the main purpose I bought it for.

title: Should be called a ‘wet bag’
text:
I am absolutely disgusted with this purchase and feel completely misled by the product description. I bought this item expecting a high-quality, waterproof container for my sports gear, specifically for carrying sweaty towels and damp clothing after intense workouts. Instead, what arrived in the mail is a pathetic excuse for a bag that does exactly what it should not: it leaks. Calling this a proper storage solution is a joke; it should honestly be classified as a "wet bag" in the worst possible sense of the term, meaning it is useless for its primary intended purpose.

The material feels incredibly cheap and flimsy from the moment you take it out of the package. It lacks any structural integrity, making it difficult to stand up on its own, which is a basic requirement for a gym bag. More importantly, the stitching along the seams is incredibly poor. I only used it once, for about thirty minutes while carrying a slightly damp towel and a change of clothes, and by the time I reached my car, water had seeped through the bottom and wet the entire contents of my other bags. This is not just a minor flaw; it is a complete design failure.

Furthermore, the zipper is a nightmare. It constantly gets stuck, requiring a level of patience and force that I never expected to exert on a simple accessory. Halfway through my walk home, the zipper slid down on its own, spilling wet laundry all over the pavement. This is humiliating and inconvenient. I tried to contact the seller to request a refund, citing the obvious defects, but they have been completely unresponsive. It is frustrating to spend money on a product that feels like it was thrown together in a factory with no quality control whatsoever.

Do not waste your hard-earned money on this item. There are countless better alternatives available at the same price point that actually offer true water resistance and durability. I am left with a soggy mess and a bag that is now too damaged to use for even dry storage. If you value your time and your belongings, steer clear of this product. It is not worth the hassle, the disappointment, or the additional cost of cleaning up the mess it inevitably creates. I am giving this one star because it is the minimum allowed, and honestly, if I could give zero stars, I would. The product is fundamentally broken and fails to meet the most basic expectations of a functional sports accessory.

text: I honestly wasn’t sure what to expect when I ordered this product, largely because I had seen conflicting opinions online about its texture and efficacy. After finally using it for about two weeks, I feel like I have a pretty balanced perspective to share with you all. The primary selling point for me was the marketing claim that this could double as both a facial treatment and a hair conditioner. Unfortunately, this split personality is exactly where the product falls short for me. When I tried applying it to my face, the texture was far too abrasive. It felt less like a gentle exfoliant and more like crushed rock, which left my sensitive cheeks feeling irritated and slightly red the next morning. I have dry skin, and this definitely stripped away any natural oils, making my complexion look dull rather than radiant. I almost returned it because of that experience, but then I decided to give it another chance on my hair. This is where the product actually shines, quite literally. My hair is thick, curly, and notoriously difficult to moisturize. When I used it as a deep conditioning mask for my scalp and lengths, the results were undeniable. It detangled effortlessly, added serious shine, and left my curls defined without being heavy or greasy. I could feel the moisture penetrating the strands immediately. So, while I cannot recommend this for anyone looking for a gentle facial exfoliator, it is a solid addition to your hair care routine if you have coarse or dry hair. It earns three stars because it is mediocre at its marketed primary function but excellent at a secondary one. Do your research and know your skin type before committing to this, or you might end up with irritated skin like I did.

title: CHEAP and Broken after 3 days!
text:
I am writing this review because I feel completely cheated by my purchase. I ordered this item thinking I was getting a high-quality toy for my child, given the somewhat polished product images on the website. However, the reality is that this is one of the cheapest, flimsiest pieces of plastic I have ever encountered. The moment I opened the box, I could tell something was wrong. The packaging was torn and taped shut with cheap duct tape, which already raised some red flags, but I hoped for the best. The item itself felt lightweight and hollow, lacking the solid construction I expected from a premium toy.

On the first day, everything seemed okay, or at least passable. My kid played with it for a few hours without any immediate issues, though I noticed several loose seams along the edges. I didn’t think much of it, assuming it would settle in. That was my mistake. By the end of the second day, a small crack had appeared near the main hinge mechanism. I tried to gently press it back into place, warning my child to be careful, but I had no idea how fragile the material actually was. Then, yesterday, exactly three days after I received it, the toy completely broke apart. The main structural piece snapped clean off while my son was simply holding it.

It did not fall; it was not dropped; it just disintegrated from normal handling. This is not durability; this is a complete failure of product quality. I have bought much cheaper toys before that lasted for years, and this item cost more than half of those, yet it has already become trash. I tried to contact customer service, but the response time is slow, and I fear they will blame user error, which is absurd. I cannot recommend this to anyone. If you are looking for something that will actually last through playtime, avoid this at all costs. You are throwing your money away on a product designed to break immediately. I am deeply disappointed and will never buy from this seller again. The lack of basic integrity in the materials is unacceptable for a toy meant for children. Save your money and look elsewhere for a better, safer, and longer-lasting option.

title: Opened my EYES!
text:
I am writing this review because I feel compelled to share how profoundly this book shifted my perspective, something I haven't experienced in years of reading. As a professional who thought they had seen it all, I approached this title with a healthy dose of skepticism. I expected generic self-help clichés or superficial advice that we all encounter daily. Instead, what I found was a rigorous, beautifully structured argument that challenges the very foundations of how we perceive reality. The author does not just tell you to open your eyes; they provide the logical framework and the psychological tools necessary to actually do so.

The pacing is excellent. There are no filler chapters designed to pad the word count. Every paragraph serves a specific purpose, building upon the last to create a cohesive narrative that feels both personal and universally applicable. I found myself stopping frequently to reflect on my own biases and assumptions, which was an uncomfortable but necessary process. The writing style is accessible without being condescending, striking a rare balance between academic depth and conversational warmth.

What struck me most was the section on cognitive dissonance and how we rationalize our poor decisions. It was a mirror held up to my own life, revealing patterns I had ignored for decades. This is not a quick fix book. It requires active engagement and honest self-reflection. However, the payoff is immense. Since finishing this book, I have noticed a tangible improvement in my decision-making processes and my ability to empathize with people who hold different viewpoints.

If you are looking for entertainment, this might not be it. But if you are seeking genuine growth and a deeper understanding of the human condition, this book is an absolute necessity. It is rare to find a work that feels so urgently important and timeless all at once. I highly recommend it to anyone willing to do the hard work of seeing the truth.
