title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I decided to upgrade my home office setup and make the switch to this professional-grade desk organizer after using a cheap plastic tray for years. On paper, this product does everything it claims to do. The build quality is certainly an improvement over the budget options, and the aesthetic fits perfectly with my modern office decor. When it first arrived, I was impressed by the weight of the materials and how sturdy it felt on my mahogany desk.

However, the actual user experience has been a bit of a mixed bag. While the overall construction is solid, the attention to detail in the design is lacking. For a product at this price point, I expected the compartments to be more intuitive. I found that while the large slots are great for notebooks, the smaller pen holders are oddly shallow. If you use a standard fountain pen or a longer gel pen, they tend to lean at an angle or slide out entirely if the desk is bumped.

The biggest issue for me is the non-slip grip on the bottom. The product description mentions high-quality rubber feet, but in reality, they are small adhesive pads that started peeling off after only two weeks of use. Now, the metal base occasionally scratches my desk surface when I slide it to reach my keyboard. I have to be incredibly careful moving it, which defeats the purpose of having an efficient workspace.

Assembly was straightforward, though the instructions were printed in a font so small I needed a magnifying glass to read them. It took about ten minutes to put together, but one of the screws didn't thread properly, leaving a slight wobble in the main shelf.

In summary, it is a decent product that looks great from a distance, but it fails on the small, practical details that actually matter during a ten-hour workday. If you are prioritizing looks over absolute functionality, you will probably be happy with this purchase. But if you are looking for a precision-engineered tool to optimize your workflow, you might want to keep looking. It is a step up from the basics, but it doesn't quite reach the level of quality I expected for the cost. It gets the job done, but it isn't perfect.

title: Disappointing
text:
I wanted to like this book — the premise sounded promising and the cover copy promised an engaging, fresh perspective — but overall it left me frustrated and underwhelmed. I’m giving it two stars because there are moments where the author’s insight shines through, but those are too few and too inconsistent to recommend this to most readers.

The pacing felt uneven from the start. The opening chapters dragged with excessive background detail that didn’t seem to serve the plot or character development, while later sections rushed through significant events as if the author realized halfway through that there wasn’t enough space. Important relationships and motivations were sketched rather than fully developed, so when the story demanded emotional payoff, I found myself uninvested.

Characterization was another weak spot. A few characters have distinct, memorable traits, but many felt like archetypes or plot devices. Dialogue frequently reads as stilted or expository; it tells rather than shows. I appreciate books that trust the reader to make connections, but here the opposite was true — the narration sometimes over-explains, which made the prose feel clunky.

On the positive side, the writing style is competent and there are flashes of genuinely good sentences and observations. A subplot about the protagonist’s past had potential and did deliver a handful of poignant moments. The book also wrapped up with a satisfying, if predictable, conclusion that ties most loose ends.

If you’re a completist fan of the author you might find value here, and readers who enjoy leisurely reads may appreciate the detailed descriptions. For me, though, the uneven pacing, thin character development, and occasional clumsy exposition made this a disappointing read that I can’t wholeheartedly recommend.

I bought this deck hoping it would be an easy, fun addition to family game nights, but I ended up deeply disappointed. The product description implies the cards come ready to use, with everything you need. What it doesn’t tell you is that the cards arrive in several identical partial stacks that are not shuffled together at all. So instead of popping it open and playing, I had to spread every single card out and manually shuffle them together to get a usable deck. That might sound petty, but it dramatically changes the experience—this is a toy meant for convenience and quick play, not a craft project in card organizing.

The printing quality is decent and the artwork is fine, but none of that matters when the basic functionality is broken. If you have kids, forget letting them handle this right away; I had to do the tedious sorting myself to avoid them seeing duplicate groups in a row. It took me 20–30 minutes to mix the stacks properly so the game didn’t feel repetitive. I also noticed a few cards that looked slightly bent from being tightly stacked, which wouldn’t happen with a properly randomized deck.

Customer service wasn’t helpful when I reached out—their response was generic and essentially shrugged that some people prefer to shuffle themselves. That’s not the point. The product should arrive ready to play. For the price, I expected better packaging and quality control. If you’re okay spending extra time prepping the deck for play, maybe it will work for you. But if you want something you can open and use immediately, don’t buy this. I’ll be returning mine if I can. One star.

title: Live in Gratitude (Not in Greed)
text:
Concerned about "the scary stuff" in the classical Grimm's Fairy Tales, author Susan Meredith chose to rewrite in a softer style. This 2010 soft-cover, 20 page story is nicely populated with colored illustrations on about every other page. This is a story that discourages greed and encourages love and kindness.

In our story, a simple fisherman lives by the sea with his pretty wife. He loves her deeply and works long hours to provide her with nice things to make her happy, but she was never happy. What she had was never enough. One day, he accidentally caught an enchanted flounder. Lady fish "Lorraine" was a beautiful fish with big green eyes and red eyelashes. She spoke, begging for her release, explaining that she was an enchanted princess who was never happy with what she had. She wished for more and more, until she wished too much and "poof". Now she could only grant wishes for others; nothing for herself. Because of his kindness, Lorraine offered the fisherman a wish as he returned her to the sea, but he declined, saying he had everything he needed to make him happy.

Well, you guessed it! When the fisherman returned home and told his wife, she became very angry. SHE wanted more and insisted he return to the sea and ask Lorraine for a larger house. The wife got her wish, but she continued to ask for more and more. Each time the fisherman went to see Lorraine, they chatted like friends and Lorraine granted the wish. Meanwhile, the wife acted as though her husband was no longer good enough for her and her fine house, money, and servants. On his last trip, Lorraine suggested he send his wife instead, if she still wanted more. The wife came, and as you may have guessed, she wished one wish too many and "poof".

Enchanted princess Lorraine changed back to a beautiful woman and rowed ashore to the fisherman.

Without violence or scary stuff, the story illustrates karma nicely - what goes around comes around - you reap what you sow, etc. It also encourages love and gratitude, and discourages being caught up in greed over material things.

Nice value lesson for children, written well, easy to understand, pretty to look at--a winner all around. Even my inner child enjoyed the story!

text:
I wanted to like this book, despite having read O'Reilly's "Killing Patton" which contained a very thin conspiracy theory about Patton's death. "Legends and Lies" purports to be a history book but is filled with inconsistencies and inaccuracies.

For example, on page 5, the book states that "Daniel Boone was born in Pennsylvania in 1734, the sixth child of ...". Yet on page 6, in a photo apparently depicting an unidentified stone house, the cut says "... Daniel Boone was the seventh of twelve children." Which is it?

On page 67, the narrative talks about Kit Carson being attacked by a band of Kiowa Indians on November 25, 1864. "Within hours, about fourteen hundred warriors attacked. It was similar to the situation in which General Custer would find himself a few months later." But 'Custer's Last Stand' occurred on June 25, 1876, nearly twelve YEARS later, not 'a few months.'

Also on page 67, "... while the Navajos, after signing a treaty in 1868 with General Sherman, were moved to a portion of their traditional lands, where they have remained." But on the photo on the facing page, the cutline says the Navajos "...settled peacefully on this land, as negotiated by (Kit) Carson." But in 1868, Carson was in Colorado, either dead or dying, according to the same chapter.

While any history book might understandably contain discrepencies, when compared to other history books, it should not contradict itself, especially on adjoining pages. For that reason, I stopped reading this book about half-way through and consider it a waste of money.

I am not usually one to lose sleep over a paperback, but I found myself completely unable to put this book down last night. I had every intention of reading for thirty minutes before bed, but suddenly it was 1:37 AM, and I had reached the final chapter. I found myself relating deeply to the protagonist’s internal struggles, which are portrayed with such raw honesty that it felt like reading a diary entry rather than a novel. The pacing is relentless, yet never feels rushed. There are moments of quiet reflection that provide necessary breathing room, but the underlying tension never dissipates. It pulls you forward, chapter by chapter, with a momentum that makes putting the book down feel like a betrayal.

The prose itself is stunning. This isn’t just a story; it’s an experience. The descriptions are vivid without being overly verbose, allowing the imagination to fill in the gaps with crisp, clear imagery. I appreciated how the secondary characters were given distinct voices and motivations, avoiding the trap of becoming mere plot devices. They felt like real people with their own lives and agendas, which added layers of complexity to the main storyline.

What impressed me most, however, was the emotional payoff. I won’t spoil anything, but let’s just say the ending was both satisfying and heartbreaking. It stayed with me long after I closed the cover, prompting me to spend the next hour staring at the ceiling, processing the themes of loss and redemption. It’s rare to find a book that lingers in your mind days later, forcing you to re-evaluate your own perspectives.

For anyone on the fence, do yourself a favor and buy this copy. Whether you are a devoted fan of literary fiction or just looking for a gripping page-turner, this book delivers on all fronts. It is a masterclass in storytelling that respects the reader’s intelligence while delivering pure entertainment. I have already ordered a second copy as a gift for a friend who I know will have the same sleepless night I did. Five stars is not enough; if there were an option for six, I would choose it. title: World War One's Pearl Harbor?
text:
If we remember anything at all from our high school history class about why the United States got into World War I, it might have something to do with unrestricted submarine warfare. But the Zimmermann Telegram, if it was even mentioned, has long disappeared from memory, along with most of the other "facts" we learned in school. Barbara Tuchman, in this superb little book, makes a strong case for the argument that it was the revealing of the contents of this one message that convinced the American public that war with Germany was necessary.

The account reads like a spy thriller, which in fact it is. But there is not one statement which cannot be documented. Tuchman had access to American, British and German records which clearly illustrate the process of decision-making for each of the governments involved. The author has a knack for encapsulating her view of the often unimpressive character of the major players.

By 1916 World War I had degenerated into a horrible bloody stalemate from which there was no escape. Each side was desperate for fighting to end, but could accept nothing less than defeat of the enemy. None of the belligerents were prepared to consider Wilson's efforts toward "peace without victory." The only solution for the Allies was to bring the United States into the war, and for the Central Powers, to keep her out. Germany was convinced that, through unrestricted submarine warfare, against neutral as well as belligerent shipping, she could force Britain to capitulate in a few months. The Allies were hoping for a German blunder that would finally drag the U.S. into the war, and Britain did have a secret weapon of which the Germans knew nothing; she had broken the German diplomatic code and was reading all German international messages, both cable and radio. How this all played out is the theme of this little volume. It is illuminating, with respect to this important turning point in world history, and to the processes by which nations are governed.

title: Outstanding book on grief
text:
Out to Sea is the kind of book I wish I had had for my daughter when my own mother — her nana — died. Death is a hard concept, especially for young children. And memories are fleeting. It was less than a month later that my daughter said she couldn’t remember Nana’s voice. It’s been three years, and most of the memories are gone, but we still find Nana in my daughter’s smile, in our garden, in books and in our hearts.

Out to Sea explains all this in such a simple and profound way. Helen Kellock’s sparse text and encompassing illustrations speak right to child’s — or adult’s — heart. And while exploring social and emotional issues, Kellock’s use of color and movement is exceptional. I highly recommend this book for families going through the grieving process.

I also have the box of various blacks,and experimented mixing these with those on the page and ended up with profoundly 'velvety' luminousity. Like a photo of a velvet dress or curtain. Lovely. I will be buying more of these when they run out, which probably won't be anytime soon... They are large 2cm x 3 xm pans, about half full, for a total of 4-5 mm depthof driet paint. title: Great LARP helmet!!!!
text:
I bought this helmet for weekend LARP events and medieval reenactments and it has exceeded my expectations in every way. Right out of the box the fit and finish impressed me — the paint job looks like real aged metal without the cold, heavy feel of steel, and the rivet details and reinforced brow give it an authentic look that draws compliments from other players.

Comfort was my biggest concern, and this helmet delivers. The interior padding is thick enough to keep the foam cheek and forehead pieces from rubbing raw after several hours of wear, yet breathable so I don’t get overheated during intense scenarios. The chin strap is sturdy and easy to adjust one-handed, which is handy when I’m suiting up quickly. The helmet sits securely even during running and shield bashing; I never felt it shift or loosen.

Durability appears excellent — I’ve had a few decent impacts from foam weapons and some accidental drops, and the helmet has only picked up a few scuffs that add character. No cracks or structural issues. Cleaning is simple: a quick wipe with a damp cloth removes dirt and sweat stains without affecting the finish.

Sizing was accurate based on the manufacturer’s chart; I double-checked my measurements and ordered the recommended size and it fits perfectly. Shipping was fast and packaging prevented any dings in transit.

Overall this helmet gives a great balance of authenticity, comfort, and durability for LARP use. It looks great in photos, feels secure during play, and stands up to rough handling. I’d recommend it to anyone wanting a convincing, functional helmet without the cost and weight of real metal armor.

title: As advertised and helps the flat-faced pup eat with less ...
text:
I bought this raised bowl for my pug because our vet recommended we try a shallower, elevated dish to make eating more comfortable for his flat face and to reduce gulping. The product does what it says — the height is just right for him, and he seems to strain his neck less when reaching the kibble. It also appears to help him slow down a little, which is a small win.

That said, there are several things that kept me from giving five stars. The non-slip base works only on clean floors; if there’s any dust or kibble crumbs it slides a bit, and on our hardwood it moved when he pawed around. The plastic feels thinner than I expected and has picked up light scratches from washing after just a few uses. Also, the bowl depth is fine for dry kibble but not ideal for wet food or for adding water — things slosh more easily at this shallow depth.

Overall, it’s a useful, no-frills product that meets the basic need and my dog did adjust to it quickly. If you want a lightweight, affordable elevated bowl for a brachycephalic pup, this is okay, but don’t expect premium materials or a miracle for mess control.

title: Great fragrance!  Horrible shampoo!
text:
I really wanted to love this shampoo because the scent is absolutely incredible. As soon as you open the bottle, it smells like a high-end luxury spa. It has these beautiful, sophisticated notes that linger in the air and make the actual process of washing your hair feel like a treat. If I were rating this based on fragrance alone, it would be a five-star product without question. Unfortunately, a shampoo needs to actually function as a cleanser and conditioner, and this one fails miserably in that department.

The first thing I noticed was the texture. It is far too thin, almost watery, which meant I had to use twice as much as usual just to get it to lather. Even then, the lather was weak and didn't feel like it was actually lifting any oil or buildup from my scalp. After rinsing, my hair felt strangely tacky, as if there was a film left behind that wouldn't wash away.

The real disaster happened once my hair dried. I have medium-textured hair that is usually manageable, but after using this, my strands felt like straw. It stripped every bit of moisture from my hair, leaving it frizzy, tangled, and completely lifeless. I spent twenty minutes trying to brush through the knots, and I genuinely feared I was going to cause breakage. It felt as though the chemicals used to create that amazing scent completely overwhelmed the moisturizing ingredients, or perhaps there weren't any moisturizing ingredients to begin with.

I tried using a deep conditioner afterward to save my hair, but the damage was already done. My scalp also felt itchy and tight for a few hours after the wash, which makes me suspect that the fragrance is too strong or the formula is too harsh for sensitive skin.

It is such a shame because I love the way it smells, and I almost considered using it as a body wash just to keep the scent around, but for the price point, I expect a hair product to actually improve the condition of my hair. I cannot recommend this to anyone who cares about the health of their locks. Save your money and buy a shampoo that prioritizes hair care over perfume. It is a lovely scent, but a horrible shampoo.

title: Finally, a wired adapter that works with my Insignia Roku TV
text:
Have a Roku TV that is supposed to be wireless-only (why can't they include an rj45 jack anyway?). Even with a wireless router positioned right behind it, still had problems with adaptive streaming sites changing resolution streams multiple times during playback. Searched Roku forums and found an older Belkin adapter mentioned, but that's not available, and has a replacement listed that did not work for me. My son had purchased an HDE adapter for his Wii some time ago (and neglected to tell me), so I tried that and it did work with my TV. so I got one of those, too. Don't know if it was just defective, but the new one didn't work, neither on my TV or the Wii, or even on a laptop, so back it went. Still searching, because I proved to myself that something could work. Finally found this brand mentioned as working after another search, even though the seller says it doesn't. At this point, for $12 I figured what the heck. And it worked... With the other adapters not working I had tried everything, resetting to original settings, unplugging and re-plugging power, USB slot, Cat 6 cable, nothing.

With this adapter, all I had to do was unplug the power cord after installing, plug it back in, turn it on, and it worked. A little slower initial boot, but that's pretty minor to have a working wired connection with no more adaptive streaming fluctuations. Before, Netflix thought i only had 4 Mbps down on a good day, and afterward, that had tripled (according to the test in their app). With another separate speed test app, I'm actually getting as high as 54 Mbps down (out of 60 possible) now.

Edit, 6 weeks later, still using it every day, still working fine except for one incident where it didn't connect after a power on, but I just removed power again and restarted, and has been OK since.

title: Well made hat to protect against sunburn
text:
I bought this sun hat before a week-long beach trip and it has become my go-to item whenever I’m planning to be outside for more than an hour. Right out of the box you can tell it’s well made — the stitching is even, the brim keeps its shape, and the fabric feels substantial without being heavy. I needed something that would actually protect my face and neck from prolonged sun exposure, and this hat exceeded my expectations.

The brim is wide enough to shade my entire face and most of my neck when I’m standing or sitting, and it doesn’t flop down into my eyes like some floppy hats do. It has a slight wire or reinforcement around the edge that holds the shape but still allows me to fold it for packing. I was able to flatten it into my beach bag for travel and it popped back into shape perfectly when I took it out.

Comfort is another big plus. The inner band is soft and didn’t irritate my forehead even after hours of wear. There’s an adjustable chin cord that keeps the hat secure when it’s windy — I was grateful for that on a blustery coastline day. I also appreciated the ventilation panels (or breathable weave) that kept my head from getting too hot; I didn’t sweat nearly as much as I expected, even in direct sun and humidity.

Functionally it delivers on sun protection: paired with sunscreen I avoided any sunburn on my face and ears the entire trip. The color held up too — I picked a light neutral that didn’t fade after multiple outings. It’s easy to clean; a quick hand wash and air dry got rid of salt and sunscreen residue.

If I have any minor nitpicks, it’s that the sizing runs a touch large on my small head even tightened to the smallest setting, but the chin cord always keeps it snug. Also, it’s not a fashion statement — it’s clearly built for function over runway style — but I don’t mind that at all for what I bought it for.

Overall, great quality, very practical, and built to last. If you’re looking for a reliable hat to protect against sunburn during outdoor activities, this is a solid choice.

text:
I demoed this game at release, and was at first a bit daunted at the amount of apparent setup. It's not that there's a lot of setup, but if you don't sort the cards after each use, you're going to spend the first twenty minutes before playing getting them all sorted then. This seems like a 'well duh' type of comment, but remember this is a game that appeals to two types of people: card gamers (who are used to scoop and box) and those moe gamers (who aren't going to want to wait to look at the pictures). If you are planned on introducing new gamers to Tanto Cuore, I greatly recommend that you have the game setup a head of time so you can dive right into it.

Game wise, it's not the deepest strategy in the world, but you can definitely play a few interesting tricks if you really put effort into it. This again can come as a shock to some gamers. Don't be deceived: It's the maids that are attracting players, and the idea that there could be actual gameplay to go with those maids throws a number of gamers off. Drake, an artist friend, was originally in it for the breasts; when he realized he was starting to lose, all the imagery faded out of his thoughts and he could have been playing with text-only cards.

It's very much a game that sells based on the images, obviously. However, if you get past the snorts and giggles, you can find an actually fun game with just enough strategy to play. Just keep it on a high shelf if you have young ones about.

title: A captivatingly beautiful story!
text:
Tethered Angel, by T.M. Brown, is a captivatingly beautiful story, one that captures the reader like a gentle wind and takes them on a journey which must be seen to its end.
Set in the 1950’s and the burgeoning sixties, Tethered Angel follows Angel, the center of this story, an African-American teenage girl who is struggling to find her identity in a culture which is quickly changing, during an era of racism against blacks and the growing equal-rights movement under the leadership of Martin Luther King. Angel finds herself drawn away from her impoverished lifestyle by the taunts and serpentine appeals offered to her by a rich white woman. The woman convinces Angel, more by force than by reason, to travel with her to Europe, to see the world, leaving her mother behind with just a note. The story which ensues embraces the world of a young black girl at a time when racism is still pungent and violent, where people like her are treated as second-rate human beings, and where she learns to discover her strengths. Throughout the story, Angel converses with those she has lost, the dead, but her visitations from the lost and gone are more like guiding spirits, helping her through difficult times. As she grows and as her independent mind sees another road leading away from a world of bigotry and hate, Angel decides she must make it back to her mother, even years later, in spite of her new state of slavery to the rich white woman. The question is how? This is a story about courage, values, belief in oneself, and the persistence often necessary in life to climb one’s mountain. A very good read.

title: The Irish Banana Review
text:
Ask the Passengers is exactly the type of book you think you're getting when you read the summary: It's a book about a teenage girl who is trying to sort out her life and figure out who she is and who she wants to be. And yes, it has the added twist of the main character coming to terms with her sexual orientation.

I was a little surprised at how ordinary Astrid felt. Not that I expected her to be some dramatic, overblown character, but I felt like there was nothing spectacular that set her apart from a lot of the other teenage girls I read about in contemporary novels. Her parents don't get her--her mom is more concerned with her sister and her dad is fairly oblivious. That just felt formulaic to me. Aside from the lesbian angle to the story, Astrid felt like any other girl dealing with feelings for that special someone, but unsure of how to express them.

This book is all about emotion. I expected that going in, and A.S. King really does a nice job of expressing those emotions. She phrases things splendidly, and I truly enjoy her writing style. The story flowed nicely. It wasn't overly long or excessively wordy, which could have been an easy pitfall to stumble into.

Overall, this book was exactly what I expected, but that's what disappointed me. I was hoping for something that would wow me. Something I could get really excited about and sink into. The setting is a small town where everyone knows everyone's business, but again, that just felt so done already. I feel like I've read variations of this novel before, but the way King wrote it kept me engaged to the end.

empty them frequently. The unit that is in our trailer is unheated and
will occasionally freeze up during the winter; it continues to run but
the vents get covered in ice so no more moisture collects in the water
tank. But we bring it into the house and, after the ice thaws, the unit
resumes normal operation. We'll continue to use this product and
replace them as needed, but now I spend the extra $1 or 2 for the
extended warranty (which I haven't had to use yet). Overall, I would
rate this product as a 4 on a scale of 1-5, 5 being the highest. The
only reason I don't give it a 5 is the high failure rate and not being
able to figure out whether the failure is in the unit itself or in the
power supply so that the entire unit doesn't need to be thrown away when

text:
I’ll be honest, I was a bit hesitant to purchase this game initially. I had seen a few other options on the market that promised similar mechanics but were significantly more expensive, and I didn’t want to spend a fortune just to see if my family would actually enjoy it. However, after reading some of the positive feedback and seeing the reasonable price tag, I decided to take the plunge. I am so glad I did, because this product has completely exceeded my expectations in almost every way.

The first thing I noticed upon opening the box was the quality of the components. The pieces feel sturdy and well-made, not flimsy like some cheaper alternatives I have tried in the past. The cards are thick and durable, which is crucial for a game that will be played repeatedly. The board itself is vibrant and clearly printed, making it easy to read even from across the table. It’s these small details that often make or break a gaming experience, and here, they are handled perfectly.

We played our first session last weekend with some friends, and the learning curve was surprisingly gentle. The rules are explained clearly in the manual, and we were up and running within ten minutes. The gameplay is engaging and strategic without being overly complicated. It struck a nice balance between casual fun and tactical depth, which meant that both the competitive gamer in our group and the more laid-back players felt included and entertained. There were plenty of moments of laughter and friendly debate, which is exactly what I look for when gathering people together.

For the price point, this is an absolute steal. I have played games that cost three times as much that were not nearly as fun or well-designed. This game offers tremendous value for money. It is versatile enough to be played with small groups or larger parties, and the replayability factor is high because no two games seem to play out exactly the same way. If you are on the fence about buying this, do not hesitate. It is a fantastic addition to any game night collection, offering hours of entertainment without breaking the bank. I have already recommended it to several other friends and family members, and I anticipate buying a second copy for my parents soon. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a fun, high-quality game that fits within a reasonable budget.

title: Where to begin...
text:
I have never before read a book where the author is so shamelessly self-promoting as Chris Brownfield. As another reviewer previously pointed out, his arrogance removes most (if not all) of his credibility, and makes this book very difficult to enjoy. For someone who was clearly not an outstanding JO (not by a long shot), he has way too much criticism and not enough respect for his fellow Navy submariners.

For a book titled "My Nuclear Family", Brownfield spends a lot of time talking about his IA in Iraq and his problems with the US government and the War on Terror. All organizations, particularly the US government has it's fair share of problems, however I hardly consider a sub JO an expert on politics or the intricacies of war. His claims that submarines are obsolete in today's Navy only further demonstrate his ignorance on the subjects.

I was led to read this book because I am quite familiar with the Navy's nuclear training pipeline and the job requirements of a submarine JO. As such, I was most interested in the first part of Brownfield's book which focuses on his time as a JO on the USS Hartford. It seems to me that Brownfield was a sub-standard officer at best, and is now a disgruntled ex-employee of the Navy who wanted to write a bitch-fest about how difficult his job had been while simultaneously making himself out to be the lone person deserving of respect in a profession he believes to be fallen.

I wouldn't recommend this book to anyone. The officers currently serving in our sub force are an important part of our national defense and are very deserving of our respect and gratitude, despite what Brownfield thinks.

This was designed rather poorly. The 1/4" rubber hose (Pump-Manifold Connector) lays across the motor and leaves a rubber residue from the vibrations wearing down the rubber. The main outlet nozzle should not be facing over the heat sink, it should either be reversed so the Pump-Manifold Connector points away from the pump, or it should not be angled, and should instead point directly up. The Pump-Manifold Connector is also cut just exactly short enough so that the manifold is constantly vibrating against the heat sink as well. It could have been a few millimeters longer and it wouldn't cause such an annoying racket.

If someone were to put forth an effort to consciously make this product worse, I'm not sure they could succeed. It seems like someone sat down with the goal of making a frustrating product.

title: Chop Suey Culture
text:
If you like Chinese food, you should read this book. It will tell you everything you should have wondered about chop suey, fortune cookies, the Chinese restaurant industry and the Chinese people who have brought more than food to the United States

Ms. Lee uses her healthy curiosity and excellent research skills to study something we generally take for granted -- Chinese food is so unbiquitous as to be invisible, except when we're hungry. Being the daughter of Chinese immigrants and a New York Times reporter gives Ms. Lee the right lenses for studying her subject and produces insights that are subtle, interesting and thought-provoking. For example: How best to know the actual output of a Chinese restaurant when thinking about buying it? Count the garbage bags in the alley. Why were did Chinese laundries and restaurants survive 19th Century bigotry against the Chinese? Because cooking and washing were women's work and didn't threaten the white male labor force.

Equally as good as Ms. Lee's insights is her writing style. She has a tone that is a bit ironic, a bit whimsical. She appreciates the goofiness of what she is investigating, but also treats the topic respectfully. These are fine balances for a writer to maintain. And she brings many of her points home with a tidy turn of phrase: "Young professionals loved the idea that food could come from a phone rather than a stove." Or, "Common wisdom from one culture is perplexing in another." Or, finally, by describing American soy sauce as a "Frankensauce chemical counterfeit."

title: a refreshingly authentic journey
text: Rachel Held Evans' A Year of Biblical Womanhood is a refreshingly authentic story of how one woman set aside a year of her life to seek to understand and live by many of the Bible's instructions for women.  Rather than approach the biblical text from cover to cover, she devoted herself to a new topic each month.  As she researched each topic, she crafted a to do list that guided her efforts. Held Evans' honesty about her Evangelical upbringing, conversational tone, willingness to take many of the Biblical guidelines to their literal extreme, and inclusion of how she and her husband felt about many of the experiences invites the reader to enter into the story both to observe her actions and explore one's own views on what it means to be a "biblical woman."  Ultimately, her experiences lead her to a new respect for the Bible, an increased openness to considering motherhood, and an understanding that the idea of a "one-size-fits-all formula for how to be a woman of faith is a myth" (p.291-295).

text: According to the blurb in the front of the book, Bernard collaborated on this book with his wife, Judy Cornwell under the name Susannah Kells.  What resulted is a book that has all of Bernard's customary attention to historical detail, primarily told from the perspective of a much younger and idealistic viewpoint than his typical protagonists- a girl named Dorcas (Campion) Sythe. While the general romantic template is present (i.e. girl falls in love, girl thinks love is impossible, girl fights for love, etc) Cornwell's talent for intricate plot lines, complex villains, and sudden plot twists are present as well.  There were a few times in reading when the sudden switch from Campion's rosy love-filled perspective to a more jaded viewpoint (usually ending in someone's sudden and brutal death) was a little jarring, but on the whole it was still the type of read I expect when I pick up Cornwell's books- A little softer around the edges maybe, but still crafted with his trademark knack for historical realism and ripping good yarns.

title: A pleasant read, but could have been much better - 3.5 stars
text:
Meet the Essex sisters: four Scottish ladies recently orphaned and left impoverished with no prospective husbands. Now wards of the perpetually inebriated Duke of Holbrook, their first mission is to marry off their eldest, the witty and sensible Teresa, or Tess, as she prefers to be called.

Growing up without the proper training that other ladies of their kind receive, Tess knows that she must marry in order to support her sisters. But what she didn't expect is that she will immediately catch the eyes of two very eligible English gentlemen. There is the Earl of Mayne, who seems to genuinely like her and whom she will most likely develop a nice, though not passionate, affection for; and then there is the very rich, though just a mere Mister, Lucius Felton, who unnerves her and whose very nearness makes her heart somersault. While Tess knows that either man is a good choice, she is torn when both men ask for her hand in marriage.

While the story started off with a great promise, the focus on establishing the characters of the four sisters overshadows what could have been a really delightful romance between Tess and Lucius. Just when you think we'd finally get some action going between the main characters, the heroine would be involved in her sisters' dramas and so the focus is once again taken away from the romance. However, the interactions between Tess and Lucius when we finally get to the part are rather sweet, and at times, funny. The little banter we get to see between them surely adds to the delight of the story.

Overall, MUCH ADO ABOUT YOU is a pleasant read and holds promise for the stories of the other Essex sisters. Next are KISS ME, ANNABEL (Annabel's story) and THE TAMING OF THE DUKE (featuring Imogen).

title: Good, even-handed account of Davis' flight
text: The Long Surrender is a good book with the wrong title, because Jefferson Davis certainly did not surrender.  This book chronicles the events beginning in April of 1865, when Lee surrendered and Richmond fell.  Jefferson Davis and his entourage fled with the remaining treasury.  The author gives a well-researched and even-handed account of the flight of Davis.  It captures his determination to somehow rally the remaining forces and continue the war, despite the advice of his generals.  I bought this book because I wanted to understand Davis better and learn what is known about his postwar days.  It's a bit dry, but nevertheless interesting.  Davis spent two long and miserable years in confinement, and was treated inhumanely by his captors.  It recounts the anguish of his wife and her efforts to obtain at first better treatment and finally his release.  The book is chock full of little known facts about this dark period of history.  It gives a fairly detailed accounting of the Confederate treasury and the personal funds of Davis.  There is no glossing over the flaws in judgment and intransigent attitute of Jefferson Davis, but the book also illuminates his courage, conviction, and many good qualities.  For those who want to see the bitter end of his "presidency" this book is a must.

title: Reliable printer and a good value
text:
I’ve been using this printer in my home office for about three months now and overall I’m very pleased with its reliability and value. Before buying I was primarily looking for something that would handle a moderate amount of printing — invoices, shipping labels, a few flyers, and the occasional photo — without fuss or a lot of maintenance. This model has mostly delivered on that promise.

Setup was straightforward. The software package included everything I needed and the wireless setup with my laptop and phone was quick and stable. I liked that the control panel is simple; no confusing menus or tiny icons. It connects to my network without dropping out, which was a major plus compared to a previous model I owned.

Print quality is good for everyday documents. Text comes out crisp and dark, and the pages are well-aligned. Color prints are decent for internal use—presentations and handouts look professional enough—but if you want gallery-quality photos, a dedicated photo printer would still be the better choice. Print speed is reasonable for a home office; large jobs take some time but nothing excessive. I appreciate that the printer doesn’t make a lot of noise during operation.

One of the strongest points is reliability. I’ve had very few paper jams and the ones that did occur were easy to clear thanks to accessible panels. Ink usage seems efficient; I get a fair number of pages per cartridge. Replacement cartridges aren’t the cheapest on the market, but they are competitively priced and easy to find, which reinforces the overall value proposition.

There are a couple of minor drawbacks. The mobile app is functional but lacks a few advanced features I’ve seen with other brands, and occasionally the scanner takes a second try to capture documents perfectly aligned. Also, while the machine supports automatic duplex printing, it sometimes hesitates on thicker paper types.

For the price point, this printer hits most marks: dependable, easy to use, and cost-effective for regular office tasks. I’m giving it four stars rather than five because of the few small quirks and because it’s not the absolute best choice if your primary need is high-end photo printing. If you need a solid, no-nonsense printer for everyday office work, this is a very good option.

title: Cute Counting Book With Wonderful Illustrations
text: The best thing about "10 Turkeys in the Road" is indeed the turkeys, along with the rest of the illustrated material.  The artwork is superb - colorful, whimsical, and downright funny.  In this counting primer, a farmer's path becomes blocked by 10 turkeys.  The frustrated farmer tries everything to move the turkeys out of his way, but can manage to clear only one turkey at a time from his path.  Preschooler's will undoubtedly love the winsome pictures, and engaging them in the turkey counting shouldn't be difficult.  If there is any criticism to be made, however, it would be the slightly less engaging poetic narrative.  Another well-known counting book, "Five Little Monkeys Jumping on the Bed," offers a significantly more memorable poetic experience by way of it's almost sing-song verse: "Five little monkeys jumping on the bed, one fell off and bumped his head; mama called the doctor and the doctor said, 'No more monkeys jumping on the bed!'"  I've read that one with both of my kids over the years, and the catchy rhythm & rhyme of its language make it a classic.  This book doesn't quite match that one with it's poetry, but the superb illustrations make it worthwhile.  A fine choice for little ones working on their counting skills.

title: Alternative history strategy with a dash of random dice rolling
text:
As others have mentioned, Dust is like a beefed-up version of Risk where you can drop Mechanized Armor Units from the sky and send strategic bombers on a grand tour of alternate history WWII. It's fun, it's easy, and it requires just enough imagination and skill to keep you interested for hours.

The game itself comes with 2 rule books and about a million game pieces. The good news is, these pieces are actually kind of fun and more often than not you'll find yourself organizing units together as your opponent figures out his next move. Dust also comes with two different rule books, one for Premium and one for Epic. This is just shorthand for "long game" and "longer game". Along with these items, players also use cards to determine what types of moves they'll make and what special abilities they'll be able to bring into play with each turn.

If I only had one complaint with the game it's that it doesn't really capitalize on its theme all that much. Sure you get a great map of the apocalyptic future-scape, a ton of pieces representing everything from submarines to Mechs, and a card system that provides some pretty great artwork, but overall the whole idea of this "alternative history" World War II is all in your head. You don't really follow any stories, so most games end up being a large-scale RISK that doesn't suck as much as its predecessor.

All in all, I recommend this game for nothing else than being fun and entertaining.

I rarely write reviews, but I had to for this one — Opened my EYES! completely changed how I look at my daily life and the choices I make. From the first chapter I felt like the author was speaking directly to me: clear, compassionate, and unafraid to challenge common assumptions. The blend of personal anecdotes and practical exercises made the ideas land in a way that was both emotionally resonant and immediately useful.

What surprised me most was how accessible the writing is. Complex concepts are explained in straightforward language, and the short reflection prompts at the end of each chapter helped me turn insight into action. I started small — just a five-minute breathing practice and a couple of the suggested journal questions — and already noticed a shift in my focus and patience. Several passages made me pause and reconsider long-held habits, and the “reality check” sections were gentle but incisive.

The pacing is excellent; the book moves quickly enough to stay engaging but contains enough depth to be worth revisiting. I also appreciated the resource list at the back — books, apps, and websites that expand on the topics covered. The author’s voice feels trustworthy and grounded, not preachy, which made it easy to accept the tougher suggestions.

After finishing it, I gifted copies to two friends because I genuinely thought they would benefit. If you’re open to looking at your life with a little more clarity and intention, this book is a must-read. Five stars.

title: This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year
text:
This was one of the better books I’ve read so far this year. It was a nice surprise, being a debut novel about parenthood: it could have gone either way.

As the synopsis says, this is a character-driven story, and that’s what makes it so interesting and enjoyable. These are people that any toddler parent knows all too well. If you’ve ever been in a playgroup or online parenting forum/group, you can relate on some level to this book (albeit an extreme version of reality). It’s a look into modern parenting, in a yuppie world where everyone is following their own “parenting truth” and trying not to judge (though failing at doing so) others’. It is also a window into the complexities of “early-mid”adult life (if you can all it that)- relationships with others and with ourselves, and what is most important for each of us.

This book will make you smile, cringe and even think a little bit. What are the sacrifices we make for our families, for our loved ones, for our children? What are the personal costs? What wouldn’t we do to find some meaning behind the every day mundane? What is the difference between friendship and support?

I recommend it for any parent of young(ish) kids looking for an enjoyable summer read.

UPDATE 08/12/2018 REPLACED BELT

After about a year of daily use I noticed a black powder accumulating on the ground under the belt cover. I figured out it was the belt wearing out. I purchased a new one (OEM PN 5PK1320). I couldn't find any instructions on the Sunny site but it's not that hard. Remove all the screws from the belt cover, including the one that holds it in place on the left side of the bike. You might have to remove the right pedal to get the cover completely off. Once you have the cover off, remove the 10-mm retaining nuts on the two eyebolts that align the flywheel, then loosen the two 19-mm nuts that hold the flywheel in place. Lift the flywheel far enough up to slip the old belt out and the new belt in. Align the belt on the front pulley and reattach the 10-mm eyebolts to the frame, then tighten the 19-mm flywheel bolts. Place the belt on the back pulley as far as you can get it, then turn the crank to get it on the rest of the way, the same way you get a chain back onto a bicycle chain ring. Put the cover back on and you are done.

I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to sit down and share how profoundly it changed my understanding of politics. What I appreciated most was the balance: this is not polemic or partisan sloganeering. Instead, it's an invitation to think critically about institutions, incentives, and the incentives of the people who operate within them. The historical context and case studies are carefully chosen and well-researched, yet rendered in an approachable style that never talks down to the reader. I learned new frameworks for evaluating policy proposals and interpreting political behavior, and those frameworks have already changed how I read the news and discuss politics with friends.

The book is also practical — it offers tools for civic engagement that are realistic rather than utopian, which I found refreshingly honest. If you care about understanding why political systems behave as they do and want to be better informed (not just louder), this is one of the most enlightening books on the subject I've read. Highly recommended.

title: Outstanding little pump at fair price/switch is questionable
text:
UPDATE: April 2016 -- I've been using this pump for a little over a year and the pump, itself, continues to function well but I'm beginning to have problems with the float switch. The switch now turns the pump on in the full off position but, if I raise it I/2 inch, it turns off. It will restart gain at about 1 1/2 inches up or floating. I've managed to keep it working by holding it above the full off position with a rope but I'm now concerned that the rope will float away and the pump will run until it burns up or destroys the battery by running it until it is totally discharged. It appears to find a quality float switch, I'll have to spend about as much for the switch as I have for the switch and pump combo and the add-on pump. I'm still very pleased with the pump. It does what it's supposed to and does it well.

This is a strong pump for its small size and low cost. It took about fifteen minutes to pump out a twelve foot Portabote that was three quarters full of water and it's worked without fail since I installed it to keep the boat rain water free. At just over $20 for the pump and switch with an additional backup pump as a $5 add-on, this is a super bargain. So far both pump and switch have proven to be reliable but they're not designed for heavy duty use and I would not think of using them in situations where the vessel will be unattended for a long period of time or when large volumes of water need to be dealt with. While the pump can clear a significant amount of water quickly, it's really designed for light incidental use. I'm very happy with this purchase because I believe that I'm using the pump and switch as they were intended...in a non-critical situation to handle incidental rainwater and spray. To ask them to do much more could be asking for trouble.

title: Beautiful Photos - Good Healthy Recipes
text:
Mediterranean food has a reputation for being not only delicious, but healthy. The diet is rich in fruits and vegetables as well as healthy oils and lean meats and fish. There are dozens, maybe hundreds of good Mediterranean cookbooks out there, and one that is excellent and includes a huge number of recipes for variety is 1000 Mediterranean Meals: Every Recipe You Need for the Healthiest Way to Eat by Valentina Harris. This cookbook has everything: appetizers, side dishes, soups, salads, mains with or without meat and even desserts. Although they are touted as healthier dishes, they are still mouthwatering, and no one will suspect that eating them will contribute to better health.

Almost all of the recipes include a photograph, which makes the book appealing. Most cooks want to know what the dish should look like. The recipes are written in the classic style with a list of ingredients and easy-to-follow instructions that cooks at all levels can successfully make them.

The variety of the dishes is vast, and there is something for every taste. Most of the recipes include several variations to that everyone can individualize them to their personal tastes. The recipes come from several of the twenty-one countries that border the Mediterranean Sea. Popular classics are included, such as Hummus and Tzatziki, as well as some unique dishes like Huevos Revueltos and Egyptian Sweet Couscous.

Anyone who likes Mediterranean food will love reading and cooking from this excellent cookbook. There will be dozens of recipes that appeal to almost every cook.

Special thanks to NetGalley for supplying a review copy of this book.

title: Could be better.
text:
I own 4 of these bottles of varying sizes. One of them is the BPA free version. I have never liked the rubber bite valve and have always taken them off right away. There is a rubber flap that covers the air intake hole that prevents water from getting out. The downside to this is it also prevents air from getting out when the bottle is just sitting. When there is cold water in the bottle and it sits at room temperature and warms up, the water expands and leaks out the main valve. A solution is to remove the little rubber flap that covers the air intake hole but this makes it more prone to spilling when the bottle tips over.

Two of the bottles (both older 0.5L) seem to have a small opening and very little water comes out no matter how hard I suck on it. There appears to be two moving rubber parts in the mouthpiece that get stuck easily and no amount of cleaning gets them to work properly.

One bottle (newer BPA free 1L) the mouthpiece turned orange for no particular reason. It doesn't affect the performance, it just makes it look dirty when it isn't. That same bottle the lever to flip up the valve broke off. I have never dropped the bottle, it just broke off from regular use.

This leaves only 1 bottle (older 0.75L) out of 4 that I haven't had any problems with.

I have written to the email on their website about warranty claims and have never even received a response from them.
(edit: I did eventually get 2 new caps after a couple emails and they seem to be working fine but the water flow still seems slower than the older cap I have that still works. It looks like they changed the design some and possibly reduced the opening.)

Overall I love the bottle that works and wish they would all work like they are suppose to.

title: Skillful, witty and caring
text:
I was delighted to find this author, known for his travel narratives and splendid prose, an Englishman born in 1908 and only dying recently at age 95 in Saffron Walden, Essex, where he had lived modestly and politely, shyly even. Luigi Barzini described reading his prose as "like eating cherries" and Graham Greene - with whom Lewis shared many similarities in adventures, courage and quiet, commanding prose - had "no hesitation in calling him one of the best writers, not of any particular decade, but of our century".

In this work - part of a multiple volume autobiography, there was only one decision Lewis made that damaged his intellect in this readers view - he agreed to an investigative reporting trip to Peru accompanied by Lord Snowden as his photographer, traveling "incognito". Lewis seemed genuinely surprised that was far from a successful trip, or experience, and as for the `incognito' - well at least it got the author free upgrades to First Class flights and entertainment by British Ambassadors and Peruvian society!

The author had a fascinating and often wildly exciting life, serving in the British Forces in Italy during WWII followed by a career in journalism reporting on Vietnam, Burma, Indo China and producing a splendid series of books for Jonathan Cape - who used to entertain his authors with dinners of burnt Irish Stew - on the mafia in Sicily, and the threatened indigenous peoples of Latin America.

Writing with a compassion and light wit Lewis crafted over thirty books and one of his five children, his second son Gareth, has also published a book called 'Deceit'.

text:
I have played this game both as a play tester Storyteller and Player for many years now, and I love it. Everyone (especially the stalwart Dungeons & Dragons players disappointed with the watered down D&D latest editions) loves the game system and basic premise: to become emperor at all costs (even at the expense of the other players). In that respect, it's like Celebrity Apprentice or Survivor in that the players work together but all are really scheming to outdo each other to eventually rise to such power as to become Emperor or Empress.

The whole game has an open spell system (this book [[ASIN:0692088644 The Adventurer's Rulebook: An Essential Component of the Immortal Empires Role-Playing Game for Mature Players]] ) where you create your own spells with a straightforward point system, 10 huge magical fighting arts (this book and the Storyteller's Codex) with 40 fighting art powers each, nonmagical Talents for fighters and thieves, politicians and assassins, and much more.

The system uses d10s only, and the opposed roll system is perfect. It allows the weaker characters a chance against the great characters, as in real life. Overall, it's a great game, in my humble opinion, and a great learning tool for math, vocabulary, and yes, even Latin!

To get a feel for the game, because it is costly (but it is well worth it as these are premium 8.5x11" full color laminate hard cover books), people should order the three available novels:

title: Adequate Brush But Buyer Beware
text:
I first purchased this brush back in 2013. After just a few shaves the brush separated from the handle and I started a return. I wanted a replacement, but it was out of stock so Simply Beautiful sent me a refund instead, without requiring me to return the defective brush. I decided to attempt a repair of the brush. After gluing it back together with marine epoxy the brush is still working fine but showing it's age through normal wear. Now five years later (2018) I decided to purchase a backup to have on hand for when the old brush becomes worn out. So I ordered a second brush thinking by now the manufacturer had probably worked out the issue. Unfortunately, again after just a few uses the new brush also separated from the handle. This time the seller, Simply Beautiful, sent me a replacement. The replacement seems to be performing fine after a few weeks of usage. So far, so good.

In summary, I like the brush. It suits my needs. But I am disappointed in the manufacturing of the product.
If you order one of these be prepared for this issue. And maybe have some Marine Epoxy on hand.

As a side note, it is not unusual for some brushes to have a "wet dog" odor when new. This can be remedied by repeatedly soaking the brush in soapy water overnight. Through normal usage the odor will eventually go away.

title: A shamanic journey
text:
In this seventh instalment of Stoner's (and friends') adventures, Stoner and her business partner Marylou have moved their travel agency from Boston to Shelburne Falls. This small New Age town is perfect for Aunt Hermione's psychic activities and a new start for teacher Gwen, Stoner's life partner. But is seventy-five-year-old Hermione eventually getting old, or is her forgetfulness caused by hungry ghosts trying to steal her soul? It is up to reluctant believer Stoner to take a shamanic journey and save her aunt.

While previously her adventures mostly involved down-to-earth detective work on the side, Stoner is no stranger to shamanic journeying ('Grey Magic') and has even experienced time travel ('Captive in Time'). However she'd rather have a normal day-to-day life even if she feels like something is missing, despite Gwen's devoted love.

'Shaman's Moon' carries the trademark humour and feminist ideas of the Stoner McTavish series, even if no one is perfect. This volume, first published in 1998, is infused with light touches of philosophy and a dose of Native-American spirituality. It is captivating and colourful, and I guess would be pivotal in the series if Sarah Dreher had written more. I believe there is an 8th volume ('Love Murders'), but it is out of print or unavailable.

Sadly the author died in spring 2012. I'll be forever grateful to Sarah Dreher for creating one of my favourite fictional characters: the neurotic –but lovable, and forever hypothesizing too much, Stoner McTavish, a womon weary of cats, devoted to her aunt Hermione, passionately in love with her partner Gwen, and generally understanding of her best friend Marylou.

If you liked Spitzer's "Riding the Unit", you'll most definitely enjoy this more. In some ways, the irreal-ist quality of these shorts, wondrously masked by trademark obscenity, turns The Art of Fiction (1984) on its ear. Again, maybe.

title: Felt like a boss shutting down sector 12
text:
Had your emotional subroutines removed? Got an unproductive sector? Fret no more! Shockwave is here to shut them down and toss those unproductive Decepticons over to Project Nemesis where they're needed. He's small enough to fit in your pocket so you can stroll around Cybertron with him to keep those other sectors in line. War for Cybertron reference aside....

PARENTS: This is an awesome little toy for young and adult Transformers fans. Shockwave is this character's name and he is one of the primary villains (Decepticon team) in the Transformer shows. He's basically 2nd in command to Megatron (the chief villain/antagonist). This Shockwave model is only 13 steps to transform, which may prove difficult for young children who are inexperienced with Transformer toys. For those children, I'd recommend the 1-step line of toys (Cybertron Adventures and Rescue Bots). My 4 year old has a lot of exposure to my complex Transformer collection, so he powers through 13 steps without a sweat. Note that the hand cannon is detachable, so be wary of losing this to the couch cushion abyss like the rest of your kid's toy accessories. Lastly, this is a "core class" figure, so it's relatively small at 3.5" when standing in robot mode.

My opinion of this model is very positive. For such a small scale, the sculpting work is super detailed and it does a near perfect job of capturing Shockwave's "Gen1" appearance (except for the angry brow). His robot-mode transformation is engineered well, tight joints/pivots and no fear of breaking any brittle pieces. The alt-mode (a tank?) is acceptable, but I've no major complaints about either mode.

title: A real treat to Adrien and Jake fans, and a love letter from Josh Lanyon to these beloved characters.
text:
A very entertaining, thought-provoking, occasionally emotional read.

Fatal Shadows, the first book in the Adrien English series, being so well known to Josh’s readers, seemed like the perfect choice for a Choose Your Own Adventure version, because the characters and their original trajectory are so familiar that it becomes easy for readers to experiment with and explore even the wildest alternative scenarios,
The book also presents some new characters and some unexpectedly tender moments involving them,
Moreoever, some of the most satisfying storylines in this book are IMO those where a little more is subtly revealed of a character’s emotion and thought than in the original book. It has a liberating effect, as the CYOA concept allows a lot of freedom to uncover all those fears or bottled up emotions that in the original Fatal Shadows had remained under the surface,
The illustrations by Catherine Dair are the icing on the cake :). They make the book richer (and only a print edition could do them justice) and it’s a nice nod to the original CYOA book format which includes illustrations. And they’re not just there for decoration: Josh uses them as a plot device, so they can’t definitely be missed :)

All in all, I didn't expect such a rich and inventive book. What I did expect, and was not disappointed with, was the apparently effortless way Josh Lanyon has to combine humour, dry wit and emotion in such a creative and satisfying way.

title: Wonderful Book - Looking forward to a 2nd Ed.
text:
Fr. Emmanuel does an admirable job of commenting on various liturgical questions, and does not balk at some of the more contentious issues (cf. "The Gate and the Curtain" pp. 181-2; who knew that St. John Chrysostom mentioned the use of a Curtain?!), providing multiple perspectives. It is set up as a textbook including multiple layers of depth in commentary, from the more casual student of Liturgy, to the more scholarly.

A second edition would be most welcome, as there are a number of page cross-references which are incorrect, and at least one diagram is mentioned which does not appear in the text. Much recourse in footnotes is made to electronic sources, which may simply be the direction of modern scholarship, but does evoke a double-take when used in a field that stretches back millennia.

In all, a wonderful start, and a second edition to take care of minor housekeeping issues will be most enthusiastically received.

title: What makes an Effective Teacher?
text:
10 Traits of Highly Effective Teachers by Elaine K. McEwan is well put together book, with lots of graphic organizers to clearly illustrate the ten traits. It concisely lists and explains the traits that make administrators and teachers effective. This book provides tools for teachers, administrators, and mentors to help others and themselves become more effective.
Principals and administrators will find ideas to help them improve instruction, become more able mentors, and motivate effective teachers. Teachers will find information and inspiration to define personal definitions of effective teaching. The book will give every teacher a renewed sense of mission and vision of what teaching can be.
McEwan's book divides the traits into three categories: personal traits, teaching traits, and knowledge traits. She introduces you to each trait through real-life examples, personal vignettes, and reflections of students, parents and educators. She provides many lists, questions, and exercises to empower teachers and nurture the ten traits.

I bought this electronics kit because I wanted a single package to experiment with basic circuits and small projects without buying parts piecemeal. title: Been buying these glasses for years they are cheap but ...
text:
Been buying these glasses for years. They are cheap, but honestly, they do the job for me. I have tried many brands over the last five years, ranging from the expensive designer stuff at the mall to various online alternatives, but I always seem to come back to these. The price point is unbeatable, especially when you consider that I go through a pair roughly every two years due to normal wear and tear. The frames are lightweight, which is a huge plus because I often forget I am wearing them. They do not slip down my nose even during long days at work, which is a common issue with other budget options I have tested.

However, they are not perfect. The hinges feel a bit flimsy, and you have to handle them with a bit more care than higher-end brands. I accidentally sat on one last winter, and while it survived, the arm was slightly bent. A gentle tweak fixed it, but it did remind me that these are not built for rough treatment. The lenses are clear enough for reading and basic tasks, but if you need high-precision optical clarity for driving at night or detailed computer work, you might want to invest in something with better coating quality. That said, for casual use, extra pairs for around the house, or as a backup when I travel, they are fantastic. The fit is standard and accommodates most face shapes without pinching. I appreciate that they come in multiple colors, so I can match them to my daily outfits. For the money, you simply cannot beat the value. They are disposable in a sense, but for most people, that is a feature, not a bug. I will continue to buy them because replacement is inexpensive, and they get the job done without breaking the bank. Just be gentle with them, and they will last you a good while. Five stars would be nice, but the build quality holds them back slightly from true premium status. Still, a solid choice for budget-conscious shoppers.

title: Low key clutch to have!
text:
I was initially hesitant to purchase this item because the price point seemed unusually low for office supplies of this caliber, but I decided to take a chance after reading some of the positive feedback. I am thrilled to say that I have absolutely no regrets. This low-key clutch has quickly become my most essential accessory for organizing my workspace, and I believe it offers incredible value for the money. The design is sleek and minimalist, which fits perfectly with the aesthetic of my modern home office. It does not shout for attention, but it certainly commands respect by keeping my desk clutter-free and efficient.

The material feels surprisingly durable despite the affordable cost. I have been using it daily for about three weeks now, juggling pens, sticky notes, small notebooks, and even my charging cables, and it has held up without any signs of wear or tear. The zippers glide smoothly, and the compartments are thoughtfully sized, preventing the common issue of small items getting lost at the bottom of a bag or drawer. I particularly appreciate the lightweight nature of the clutch, which makes it easy to carry around if I need to move my workstation or bring my essentials to a meeting.

For anyone looking to streamline their organizational routine without spending a fortune, this product is a no-brainer. It is practical, stylish, and functional in equal measure. The low profile means it slides easily into larger bags or sits neatly on a desk shelf without taking up too much visual space. I have already recommended it to several colleagues who were struggling with their own clutter issues. If you are on the fence about buying it, just go for it. You will likely find yourself wondering why you did not invest in good organization tools sooner. This clutch has genuinely improved my productivity by making it easier to find what I need when I need it. Five stars all the way.

title: Useless for techies
text:
I'm a developer building a company-internal website and I'm struggling to organize all the information it will contain. I bought this book hoping to ease that struggle. What I found is for a technical person like me, this book was so useless that it has compelled me to write my first Amazon review in years.

I planned to read it cover to cover. After 50 pages I realized that I haven't really read anything at all yet. So far it's been ridiculously verbose, rambling, and content-free. So I gave up and started skimming.

I couldn't find much better in the remaining pages. Page after page of touchy-feely gobbledygook that has not helped me organize information at all.

There are more useless diagrams in this book than I've ever seen before. For example, the term "synonym ring" is defined as a group of words with the same meaning. Does it really take a diagram with a bunch of arrows in a circle to explain that? (Figure 9-2)

To explain the concept of equivalence we have another diagram: "A=B" inside a circle. (Figure 9-21) Does such a diagram really enhance anybody's understanding of the concept of equivalence? Why does this diagram even exist in the first place?

Maybe some business or consultant type might get something out of this book. For a developer, run away. Fast.

I opened the first toner, installed it, and immediately noticed a strange streak down the page. At first, I thought it was just a glitch with my printer or perhaps a defective unit, so I checked the packaging for the second tonner. I replaced the first one, hoping for the best, but the second unit did the exact same thing. Both cartridges, without exception, leave thick, uneven, and undeniable dark spots all over every single document I print. It ruins important reports and makes even casual correspondence look unprofessional and sloppy. I have tried cleaning the internal rollers multiple times and reseating the cartridges, but the issue persists regardless of what I do. It is clear that these are not manufactured with any quality control standards whatsoever. The consistency of the defect across two separate units proves that this is a widespread manufacturing flaw, not a one-time accident. I expected basic functionality for the price I paid, not for my printer to act like a paintball machine. I am requesting a full refund immediately because I cannot continue using these products. Do not waste your money on this brand. Save yourself the headache, the wasted paper, and the frustration that comes with trying to explain to your boss why the quarterly report looks like it was printed through mud. This is by far the worst office supply purchase I have made in years.

This new fan is definitely weaker than my old one, and I rarely use it on the second speed and never on the lowest. Interestingly, it turns on to the highest speed and shifts lower. Some people may be disappointed to find out that's all there is. I can actually use the remote from my old fan with this model, which I like. I can keep one in each room where I may use it (it's definitely light enough to move between them), The new remote, which doesn't come with batteries, is a little less easy to use in the dark because of the buttons. And while it can hook onto the back of the fan for safekeeping, I preferred the way my old fan had a slot. The remote has a tendency to fall off. With that said, this is the third type of fan I've purchased to replace my defunct one and the only one tall enough and strong enough to work with the height of my bed and layout of my room.  I doubt this model will last over a decade, and I'd prefer if the price were under $50, but it'll do.

These are two part adapters, one piece can be left connected to the laptop and only protrudes a few millimeters out (less than my mouse receiver). The other piece can take the damage of plugging/unplugging USB devices in and out of it saving my one and only USB-C port from the damage.
The magnets on these are very strong and requires more than a little tug to disconnect them. One concern I had was "Would I get shocked by the part that remains in the laptop?" I am happy to report the electrical connectors are recessed into the connector itself while the part that disconnects has the protruding plug. In other words, the part I leave in my laptop is the female part of the adapter. So, no accidental electrical shocks.

text:
What makes this collection unique: it's printed on full-size newspaper stock
What makes this really amazing: they have taken the actual page from the newspaper of that year and reprinted it here with the ads and other articles as originally in the newspaper. You may find yourself ignoring the crossword and reading, say, the movie or book review from 1990. Or just perusing the ads.

The editors have taken one puzzle from each year back to 1942 and printed its entire page.

The downside to the book so far (I started at 2016 and worked backwards) is when you get to the Eugene Maleska years (77-93) (Oh, let me
correct myself: it's Eugene T. Maleska, not to be confused with all those other Eugene Maleska's in the USA). That "T" might tell you all you
need to know about his puzzles. They reek of what passed for knowledge way back when: obscure Broadway shows, "great" writers that most
people have never heard of, French language (by the way, there was an error in one of those), capitols of regions of small nations etc.

I have another compilation of NY Times puzzles that goes back decades which is very challenging because what passed for common knowledge back then is obscure now. However, that's not my issue with Maleska.

Altogether, this is a great gift for any crossword puzzler; mine was a gift as well.
