title: Up
text:
I bought the Up as a gift for my teenage son who’s been getting into trail running and cycling, and it’s become one of those rare purchases that actually exceeds expectations. Right out of the box the unit felt solid and well-made. Setup was straightforward — the quick-start guide was clear, and pairing with my phone took two minutes. The app is intuitive and gives useful summaries without being cluttered.

The first thing that struck me was the accuracy of the activity tracking. Steps, distance, and elevation on hikes matched the readouts on his watch and my bike computer within a small margin. Sleep tracking has been surprisingly helpful: he used to complain about feeling tired all day, but after a few nights of reviewing the detailed sleep stages and suggestions, he changed his evening routine and now reports waking up more refreshed. Battery life is strong; we go several days between charges even with nightly sleep monitoring enabled.

For someone active, the Up’s fitness coaching features are a standout. The guided goals and gentle reminders helped him increase daily movement without feeling nagged. It also integrates nicely with other apps we use for running, so we didn’t have to manually transfer data. Durability has been impressive — it’s been knocked, splashed, and worn during muddy trail runs and still looks and functions like new.

A few relatively minor quibbles: the band could be a touch softer for all-day comfort, especially in hot weather, and the vibration alerts are on the light side (easy to miss during a loud workout). Also, the app’s social/competitions features are a bit basic compared to larger ecosystems, but that’s not a dealbreaker for us.

Overall, the Up hits the sweet spot for reliable tracking, helpful coaching, and good battery life in a rugged package. My son is using it daily and his activity levels have gone up noticeably. If you want a solid, no-fuss tracker that actually helps you move more and sleep better, this one is well worth the price.

The build quality feels solid for the price. The materials don’t feel cheap; they’re lightweight and breathable so my ears don’t get hot. They also stay in place really well when I’m walking or riding the subway — I haven’t had a single near-fall or readjustment while moving around. Sound isolation is decent; they don’t block out everything but they reduce background noise just enough to make calls and podcasts clear. I’ve used them with a couple of different earbud models and they’re compatible and flexible enough to fit snugly.

If you want comfortable, reliable ear hooks with elastic straps that actually make wearing earbuds for long periods pleasant, these are a great buy. Good value, comfortable fit, and well-made — I’d definitely purchase again or recommend to anyone who struggles with ear fatigue from regular earbud use.

LaFemina rejects gratuitous allusion in favor of contemplation of the commonplace, elevating the thing-ness of things, refusing to surrender to the ordinary. There is a leitmotif that I'm not sure was a conscious choice of the poet, but it is delightful all the same: Klee's cat, Schrodinger's cat, his cat, a lover's cat, raining cats, and an apophatic mention of Eliot's cats. title: More informative than grouchy!
text:
"The Grouchy Grammarian" is not a grouchy book. Parrish's fictional curmudgeon limits his irritation to public figures and national media outlets for spreading grammatical errors and "infelicities" throughout the populace. Parrish constructively channels his alter-ego's concerns, and the result is enlightening rather than chastening. Among usage guides, this one is particularly helpful for three reasons:
1) Each topic is covered in a short chapter, and each chapter ends with a summary so you can learn a lot quickly.
2) Parrish includes a thorough index, and a thoughtful annotated bibliography of guides to language, writing and usage.
3) Parrish clearly explains why usage glitches are glitches. Now that I understand what NOT to do, I don't have to laboriously memorize rules about what to do. Rote memorization of grammar rules never worked for me--I resemble the student in "Up the Down Staircase" who complains that "semicolons don't stick to my head."
I wish all people who worry about "weak", "watery" assaults upon English had mediators like Parrish to absorb their ire and deftly convey their championship and knowledge of precise language.

title: Good to have on hand for emergencies
text:
I bought this for our car after a minor fender bender left us stranded one evening and I decided it was time to be better prepared. This kit has become the go-to item in our trunk — compact, lightweight, and thoughtfully put together. The carrying case is tough and zips securely so nothing shifts around, and it fits easily under the seat.

What I appreciate most is the selection of items. There are basics you actually need in a roadside situation: a bright emergency blanket, a sturdy reflective vest, heavy-duty gloves, a dependable flashlight with extra batteries, and a first-aid kit that contains more than just a few adhesive bandages. The jumper cables are solid and come in a pouch to keep them from tangling. There’s also a multi-tool and a seatbelt cutter/window breaker — small additions that give real peace of mind.

Quality feels good for the price. Nothing in the kit feels cheap or likely to fail when you need it. The reflective strips and vest are visible from a distance, and the flashlight is brighter than I expected. The first-aid supplies are clearly labeled and the manual included is straightforward and useful for non-medical people like me.

I’ve used a couple of items already — the blanket and gloves — and they stood up to use without issue. Even if you never need to use most of it, having this kit in your car reduces stress when things go wrong. For weekend camping or keeping in a sports bag, it’s just as handy. Highly recommend for anyone who wants a well-rounded, reliable emergency kit without overpaying.

title: Nice large scooter wheel
text:
I bought this wheel to replace a worn-out one on my son's stunt scooter, and overall, I am quite happy with the purchase. When you are looking for a larger wheel, the main goal is usually to get a smoother ride over rougher pavement and a bit more stability at higher speeds. This product definitely delivers on that front.

The build quality is impressive. The core feels sturdy and doesn't seem like it will crack under pressure during jumps or hard landings. The polyurethane material is dense and has a good grip on the road, which gives a lot more confidence when carving or turning sharply. Compared to the smaller stock wheels that came with the scooter, these make a noticeable difference in how the ride feels. The vibration from the asphalt is significantly reduced, and it takes a bit more effort to maintain speed, but it glides much further once you get going.

The installation process was straightforward, although I did have to double-check my bearings. The wheel fits perfectly on the axle without any wobbling. I noticed that the color is slightly different from the images online, but it is still a nice, vibrant shade that looks great on the deck.

The reason I am giving this four stars instead of five is that I noticed a tiny bit of flat-spotting after about two weeks of heavy use. My son tends to skid and brake hard, and while the wheels are durable, they aren't completely immune to wear and tear. I think they are great for general riding and moderate stunts, but if you are a professional-level rider doing extreme grinds every single day, you might find them wearing down faster than the premium high-end brands. However, for the price point, the value is exceptional.

If you are looking to upgrade a basic scooter to make it feel more "premium" and smooth, this is a fantastic choice. It transforms the ride from a bumpy, jittery experience into something much more fluid. I would definitely recommend these to any parent or rider who wants a larger wheel without spending a fortune. Just be mindful of how hard you brake if you want them to last as long as possible. It is a solid, reliable piece of equipment that does exactly what it claims to do.

text:
I bought this because the photos made it look charming and the size seemed perfect for a small corner by my sink. After using it for a few weeks I’m giving it three stars — it’s cute and well made in a decorative way, but it falls short as a genuinely useful kitchen item.

First the positives: the finish is attractive and matches the description. The paint/print hasn’t faded and there are no noticeable chips or defects out of the box. It feels reasonably sturdy for a decorative piece and the seams are neat. If your primary goal is to add a bit of personality to a windowsill, open shelf, or to complement a farmhouse/retro vibe, this will do that job fine. I also appreciate that it arrived carefully packaged; no scratches or scuffs.

Now the drawbacks that keep me from giving it more stars. The product is marketed as being functional for holding sponges/soap, but in practice it doesn’t drain well (if it’s designed to). Water collects in the bottom and even after draining a sponge for a while it still leaves a damp puddle. That makes the sponge stay wet and feel slimy after a few days — I’ve had to empty and dry it regularly, which defeats the point of a “hands-free” holder. If you use it for soap, the soap can end up sitting in a little pool and becoming mushy faster than I expected.

The size description was slightly misleading: it’s smaller than I pictured. It fits one compact sponge or a small bar of soap, but not much else. If you hoped to store multiple items (brush + sponge + scrubber), you’ll be disappointed. Also, there’s no non-slip base, so it slides on my counter when I grab the sponge unless I keep it on a textured tray.

In summary: attractive and decent quality for decoration, but not very practical for continuous everyday use unless you don’t mind occasional maintenance (emptying and drying). I’m keeping it because it brightens up the area, but if you need something primarily functional to keep sponges dry and neat, look for a holder specifically designed with drainage and non-slip features. This one is more about style than substance.

Customer support was responsive when I emailed with a question about replacement parts. The reply came within 48 hours and included helpful links and clear next steps, which was reassuring.

Overall, this product delivers excellent value. It balances design, performance, and price well. If you want something reliable for everyday use without spending a lot, this is worth considering. title: Items missing :(
text:
I don’t usually write reviews, but I felt I had to after this disappointing purchase. I bought this set for my seven-year-old’s birthday because the pictures and description made it look like a complete kit with everything needed to build multiple models. What arrived was missing several key pieces, and the whole experience felt like a bait-and-switch.

Right out of the box I noticed the box felt lighter than I expected. We opened it together and started sorting parts, following the instructions included. About 20 minutes in we hit a wall: essential connector pieces and what should have been one of the motor assemblies were nowhere to be found. I checked every compartment and bag multiple times, double-checked the parts list in the manual, and even dumped everything out onto the carpet to be certain. Several unique, identifiable parts that are shown in the product photos and listed as included were absent.

Customer service was not much help. I reached out via the seller’s contact page and got an automated confirmation immediately, but then silence for days. A week later I received a generic reply asking for photos and order information, which I supplied. After that, no follow-up and no resolution. I tried again to escalate through Amazon, and while they eventually offered a partial refund or a return for a full refund, it was cumbersome: I would have had to box everything back up, ship it off, and wait weeks. By then my child’s party had passed and the toy lost its purpose.

The product that did arrive looks well-made and the parts we did have seem sturdy and engaging, so I can only judge based on what was actually delivered. For the price, I expected a complete set. Missing parts render the kit unusable for the builds shown in the instructions, which was the whole point of buying it.

If you’re considering this for a gift or a project with a deadline, beware: there’s a real chance this will show up incomplete and it appears the seller may not be responsive. I’m giving one star because the product as received failed to meet basic expectations and customer service didn’t resolve the issue in any timely or satisfactory way.

title: Finally, a wired adapter that works with my Insignia Roku TV
text:
I’d been struggling for months to get a stable wired Ethernet connection on my Insignia Roku TV. Wi‑Fi kept dropping during streaming and gaming, and every “universal” Ethernet adapter I tried either wasn’t recognized by the TV or caused buffering and weird audio sync issues. I ordered this wired adapter out of desperation and it has been a night-and-day difference.

Installation was simple — plug the USB end into the TV’s USB port and plug the Ethernet cable into the adapter. The TV immediately recognized the connection without any fuss. No extra drivers, no fiddling through menus beyond selecting “Wired” instead of Wi‑Fi. Once connected, my TV showed a solid wired connection and streaming apps opened noticeably faster.

Performance-wise, it’s rock solid. 4K streaming on Netflix and Amazon Prime plays smoothly with no buffering, and online gaming feels much more responsive. I ran a speed test through the TV and the results were consistent with what I get on my wired laptop. The adapter stays cool to the touch, and I haven’t seen any disconnects after several weeks of daily use.

Build quality seems good — the connector feels sturdy and the cable is a decent thickness (not flimsy). It’s unobtrusive and doesn’t add much bulk behind the TV. My only minor gripe is that it makes the single USB port occupied, but that’s a small trade-off for reliable Ethernet.

If you have an Insignia Roku TV and need a dependable wired connection, this adapter works exactly as advertised. Finally, a wired solution that actually works with my TV — very happy with this purchase.

title: Make the switch but beware...
text:
I’ve been using these for a few weeks after deciding to switch from my old gel pens to something the office kept recommending. There are definitely pros and cons, which is why I’m giving three stars.

On the plus side, the pens look and feel professional. The barrel is solidly built and has a pleasant weight — not too light, not too heavy — so they don’t feel cheap when you hand them out in meetings. The ink dries faster than my previous pens, which is great for left-handed notes and reduces smudging. The lines are consistent at a medium thickness; good for everyday note-taking, signing documents, and printing charts. The black ink is a true black and photocopies clearly without ghosting.

However, the experience isn’t flawless. First, the grip section is slightly slippery. If you tend to write for long stretches, your fingers start to feel a bit tired because there isn’t much cushioning. Second, a few of the pens in the pack (about 2 out of 12) started to feel scratchy after a couple of weeks, like the tip wasn’t as smooth as the others. They still write, but the feel is noticeably different and a little annoying. Also, while the ink dries faster than my old pens, it still smears a little on cheaper paper stock — not a dealbreaker, but something to be aware of if you frequently use lower-quality notebooks or thermal paper.

Refill availability is another concern. The product description hinted at long-lasting cartridges, but the pens don’t appear to be easily refillable, and I couldn’t find compatible refills locally. If you plan to use these heavily, be prepared to replace the entire pen instead of just swapping a cartridge.

Overall, these pens are solid for everyday office use: they look professional, write cleanly, and mostly avoid smudging. But the inconsistent tip quality in my pack, the slippery grip, and uncertain refill options mean they’re not perfect. If you want a reliable, mid-range pen for occasional to moderate use, these are a fine choice. If you’re looking for something with an ergonomic grip or long-term refillable convenience, you might want to keep looking.

title: Mann's ambitious retelling of the Faust legend
text: Thomas Mann poured his considerable knowledge of music into this biography of fictional German composer Adrian Leverkuhn, whose musical career spans the first thirty years of the 20th century. The result is one of literature's most ambitious attempts to portray the art of music in words. At the same time, this is a self-portrait of the narrator. Writing from the perspective of 1944, like Mann himself he is a representative of an older, humanistic Germany, who looks on appalled as the Red Army marches ever closer to the German border. Hating the Nazi regime, he struggles with the fact of the national catastrophe that looms ever closer. The result is perhaps Mann's most complex novel, ironies within ironies, all contained in the story of an artist who makes a pact with the Devil (or does he? or does he imagine that he did?) in order to achieve transcendence in his art. The language is thick, the narrative moves slowly, sometimes at a snail's pace, but the complexity of the story offers rich rewards. Not for the faint of heart.

title: Sweet, slow, sad
text:
Thin Wood Walls follows young Joe Hanada's family experiences during the time of WWII. After the bombing of Pearl Harbor, Joe's father is taken away by the FBI as a person of suspicion because he is a community leader. The rest of the family, including Joe's feisty grandmother and more feisty big brother Mike, are taken to Tule Lake Relocation Camp and must adjust to a new life while anxiously awaiting the return of the father.

Not much happens in the book, as camp life is boredom, waiting, hoping, but Joe tries to make do and make sense of what is happening while fearing what his big brother intends to do. The story is balanced, showing how not all white Americans were against the Japanese in the U.S. Some Japanese were very angry while many exhibited a sad stoicism. Perhaps what sets this book apart from other internment stories is that it is set in the Tule Lake camp, which was where troublemakers, the "no-no's" and those wanting to return to Japan were sent. This created a turbulent, sometimes dangerous atmosphere that other camps did not experience, at least not on that level. Thin Wood Walls delves into this in a manner suitable for middle-graders.

The book is a bit slow, but sweet, the writing rather plain despite the bits of haiku, but this will appeal to boys as well as girls and provide a thoughtful look at the sad facts of this long-hidden part of U.S. history. Expect a tear at the end, and be sure to read the Author's Notes.

[[ASIN:0939165538 Looking Like the Enemy: My Story of Imprisonment in Japanese American Internment Camps]] is also set in Tule Lake, but is a true story. A Young Reader's edition is coming out in Fall 2010.

title: Riddle of the Book
text:
It might seem surprising, but professional bibliographers (and I am one) invariably judge a book first by its publisher. In the case of this book, it is published by Springer, a prestigious European information conglomerate. This is important because the author of this book has notably airy qualifications as a "reporter." Digital Publishing allows everyone to be an author and anyone to be a publisher, and if you can tweet you can be a "reporter." Thus, it is truly important for readers to have some sort of crap detector in place. Unfortunately, the publisher test failed on this book.

This book has virtually no redeeming substance; Wikipedia says it better -- and cheaper. The author's writing style relies on a snotty-know-it-all approach, that is particularly irritating because he has no credentials. (As an example, he even manages to insult little Corvallis, Oregon as "a jerkwater town," even though the place is a pleasantly progressive college town). Essentially, the book is about grinding axes with political correctness uber alles.

Technically, the Kindle version of the book has way too many formatting errors and unpleasant (and unnecessary) decorative images. Why ebook publishers -- and especially wealthy publishers like Springer -- can't seem to at least look at their digital product in Kindle Previewer is a bigger riddle than Kennewick Man.

My take-away from this book is that I will no longer give Springer-Verlag an automatic pass. It's easier to lose respect than to earn it, mein Herren.

title: A fantastic thriller!
text:
THE VACATION by T.M. Logan primarily follows Kate, a wife and mother of two meeting up with her three best friends and their families at a stunning vineyard villa in France for a vacation to celebrate their 40th birthdays. It is meant to be a time to reconnect with each other and their families with good wine, good food and good company. Things aren’t starting off on an ideal note, however.

Kate has a feeling that something is going on with her husband and she manages to log into his phone to check his messages. She sees a back and forth conversation which seems to confirm that her husband is having an affair. Worst yet, the messages imply that the other woman is one of her best friends. As Kate seeks to identify the traitorous friend, it is clear that all of her friends have secrets to hide.

I have been in the mood for thrillers and this one did not disappoint. Once I got into the story, I could not put it down! We are primarily reading from Kate’s POV, hearing her suspicions, seeing her interactions with her friends and family. The author also gives us occasional chapters from the perspective of other characters, Kate’s friends, their husbands and the kids as well. It seems that almost everyone has something to hide and the author does a great job of dropping clues to redirect Kate’s suspicions and the readers’ as well.

This is very much a slow burn book for the first three-quarters or so. There is a lot of family drama and mystery going on which creates that slow build up to the last quarter where things really start to happen, ramping up the thriller elements. On top of the issues of what is going on with Kate’s wife, there are clearly secrets between the teens of their families and with the other women. The slow burn is done very well and it kept me entirely hooked throughout as the author takes the time to really delve into the different characters and potential suspects for everything that is going on.

I would highly recommend adding THE VACATION by T.M. Logan to your TBR!

title: Great for documents.  Horrible for photos. Get it on sale and it's a steal!
text:
If I could do it, it would be 3.5 stars. Here is the skinny:

Pros:

Scanning and printing of normal documents is great.

You can scan to a network folder, your computer, to FTP, to a USB stick, or email as an attachment right from the printer. It's more than reasonable for first page out and multiple pages.

Easy setup. Printing from your phone is easy. Internet printing capability (print from anywhere, ready when you get home).

Toner is like all color laser printers, relatively expensive for the brand name but much cheaper than inkjet in the end.

Have been successful faxing using a OBI200 and a Google Voice number so very handy when you need to occasionally fax but don't have a physical land-line in the house.

While it isn't silent, it is not unreasonably loud. My old Canon inject makes more racket (clicks, clacks, bangs) when it starts up.

I have never had wake from stand-by issues. Wakes from sleep pretty fast.

Cons:

It is big (small con). But all color lasers tend to be in this size and up as they need to be able to hold and align all those cartridges. As a matter of fact, due to the pull-out tray design and smaller physical cartridges this is probably on the smaller side of color laser printers.

Flatbed color scanning from your computer of things like photographs, is IMHO HORRIBLE, with out of whack colors and edge diffractions and all sorts of oddities. It's to the point that I wonder if it's defective. Oddly, scanning of documents seems pretty good. I need to do some experimentation to see if it's a software driver issue or something but I've scanned direct into Photoshop, Picassa, and Acrobat and they all are pretty sub-par. The computer driver scanning controls are now very basic, not like they used to be years ago with much more control...maybe that's part of the problem.

Also, when _printing_ photographic type images the colors are massively over-saturated...okay for presentation graphs, charts, and stuff but again waaaayy off base for anything else. While I understand this is a business oriented machine, even businesses scan/print photographs and it shouldn't be this far off (a lack of functionality/settings in the printer driver could be partly to blame).

text:
The authors offer truly groundbreaking insights and methods in this book, and I will cite a few, but the depth and breadth of their work is far too vast to encapsulate here. They note the plethora of unhelpful, anecdotal advice that often passes for wisdom in similar books, and instead provide scientifically documented, step-by-step methods for defining and achieving goals. They provide compelling examples of how these techniques have been implemented. The most fascinating story, in my opinion, involved the eradication of the guinea worm, an endemic parasite that can grow up to three feet long and emerges through the skin causing tremendous pain. The authors cited techniques employed by Carter Foundation workers to teach villagers how to filter their water and prevent reinfestation of water sources by infected persons. Carter Foundation workers sought positive deviants (villages who had learned their own ways of avoiding guinea worm infestation) to teach other villages what to do.

I noted many techniques that I myself had discovered by trial and error, such as perfect practice, which involves working on improving specific elements of a task; they cite basketball freethrowing, where perfect practice includes improving followthrough, elbow position, etc., as opposed to results oriented practice that can reinforce poor technique, e.g. shoot until I get 20 baskets. As a Chemistry teacher, I inherently implemented many of these techniques. This book provided me with more insight and concrete guidance than most of the teaching and education books I was provided in my teacher training.

This is one of the most enlightening books I have ever read on human behavior. Having borrowed this book from the library, I now plan to purchase it (the actual ink and paper version), because I know I will refer to it again and again.

title: Easy and Bright
text:
I have been searching for the perfect running companion for months, and I finally found it with the Easy and Bright headlamp. As an early morning jogger, visibility is my top priority, and this product delivers exactly what it promises. The setup was incredibly intuitive, taking less than five minutes from opening the box to being ready for the trail. The instructions were clear, and the batteries included meant I didn’t have to run to the store immediately after purchase.

The brightness is phenomenal. I was skeptical at first because the lumens number seemed too high for such a compact device, but it genuinely lights up the path ahead. The beam is focused enough to see obstacles like roots and rocks but wide enough to maintain peripheral awareness. This balance is crucial for trail running safety. The red light mode is a nice bonus for preserving night vision and not blinding other runners or hikers.

Comfort is another major selling point. It sits securely on my head without any slipping, even during intense intervals or when I am sweating heavily. The adjustable strap is soft and does not cause irritation after wearing it for over an hour. I was also impressed by the battery life. I used it on the highest setting for my five-mile morning runs and only had to recharge it once every two weeks. That efficiency is remarkable.

Water resistance has held up well against light rain and morning dew, giving me peace of mind when the weather turns unpredictable. For the price point, the build quality feels premium and durable. It has survived a few accidental drops on rocky terrain without any dents or loss of function. If you are looking for a reliable, bright, and comfortable lighting solution for your outdoor adventures, do not hesitate. This is the best investment I have made for my active lifestyle this year. Highly recommended for runners, hikers, and campers alike.

title: Child of Thorn and Hunger
text:
Note: I have read the story on RoyalRoad, which goes beyond the currently published books. This review stands as a synopsis of what I have read so far.

Fantastic story heavily inspired by Vampire: The Masquerade, showcasing the unnatural dominion of vampires over humans and most other magical creatures. This includes the existence of distinct vampire clans with unique supernatural traits and an inveterate hierarchical vampire society to maintain power and secrecy.

As the main character, Ariane is painfully reborn into a warrior bloodline with an antediluvian psychopath for a progenitor. Abandoned and left to fend for herself, she must navigate the perils of vampire society as an outcast and the lawless American frontier as a woman. As much potential as she has as a vampire, her beginnings leave her weak and at the mercy of far more powerful forces. It is with intelligence and true grit that she must learn to survive and thrive.

But the real struggle for Ariane is to maintain her sense of honor and humanity as she fights against the demands of her nature and the madness of her bloodline. While far from a warrior of light, she is fearless when she chooses to fight for what she believes in and builds bonds of deep friendship with interesting and diverse people. Her acts of kindness are rare, but they shine as genuine and without the avarice and cruelty inherent to her kind.

While she definitely stumbles at times, Ariane remains steadfast to her friends and an anti-hero to those she saves along the way. I hope that her journey keeps her from succumbing to wickedness and allows her to emerge as something special. A dark star in a world of darkness.

title: Great value, particularly for the accessories
text:
Fortnite's figures are great, and collecting accessories is much of the fun, but you don't usually get many accessories with basic figures--you typically either have to buy loot chests or special/deluxe sets to get accessories. The piñatas are some of the best deals due to how many accessories you get, along with a figure. Although the MSRP of a piñata is slightly higher than the price of a single figure plus a single loot chest, you get a lot more content--over twice as many accessories as what you'd get from a standard loot chest. And not all the accessories or variations can be found in other sets--so even if you already have a decent stash of accessories, some of these will probably still be new to you.

The Rust Lord figure is not the prettiest or fanciest-looking figure in the series, but he's pretty decent. A lot of the characters are very cartoony, but this guy's design is a little bit more subdued, which may or may not be a plus depending on your tastes. Like all the 4" figures, he's got a very high amount of articulation and pretty sophisticated construction, so you'll want to be a little careful with him at first. If any joints seem stuck, try soaking him in hot water briefly to loosen them up and lessen the risk of breakage. I haven't had any problems with any of my figures yet, but be aware it can happen. I wouldn't recommend these for very young kids due to their relatively complex design.

And yes, the packaging is really a sort of piñata. It's designed for you to be able to bash it open. You can probably open it up without destroying it if you are careful. Be aware that there's a lot of confetti inside, in case you do decide to break it open.

Written by Kelly Long, "A Marriage of the Heart" tells the story of Rachel Yoder, an Amish girl who has been raised by her strict father after her mother's death. Tired of her father's and the Amish rules, Yoder quickly marries Joseph Lambert, an Amish man who has only recently returned to the Plain way. Long tells Yoder's story of falling in love with her husband and facing her demons. "What the Heart Sees" by Kathleen Fuller tells the story of Ellie Chupp, a young Amish woman who lost her sight as well as her best friend in a horrible accident. When her best friend's former fiance shows up, Ellie's attempts to deal with her disability are disrupted. However, love is just around the corner for Ellie. "Healing Hearts" by Beth Wiseman tells the story of Naaman and Levina Lapp. After 30 years of marriage, they are facing an empty nest, which is something that Naaman especially cannot deal with. He leaves for year, but when he returns he finds that things are not as he hoped they would be. Levina is cold and confused, dealing with whether or not she can trust the man who left her.

I found these three novellas to be enjoyable. Easy to read and interesting, they offer insight to the lives of the Amish, as well as insight into the lives of people in general. The stories are heartwarming and touching, and I would definitely recommend the book.

Sabaal is a captive Jakkattu imprisoned on Earth by the Mezna priests who experiment on her. Javan 6ix is a tek - half Miscegenate, half machine - beginning to question his life in the city. Norwood Thorne is too smart for a human, too inquisitive for a man, leading his sister Julip down the path of questioning the Temple, the Mezna and all the history they've learnt on the Rez.

Because beyond their fences, the Feral - the Undone as they name themselves - have information that will turn their understanding of the world upside down.

The Jakkattu Vector is action-packed, with Tyler propelling you from one scene to another, giving you glimpses of the truth, glimmers of the lies these human-Mezna hybrids have grown up with, expecting you to piece them all together before the horrifying reveal. In between, she engages your emotions with the innocence of the young Thornes as they grow up, navigating the thin line between independence and insolence in their quest for truth. And then she feeds you heartbreak on a platter.

The Jakkattu Vector is gritty and grim yet inexplicably hopeful as each of strand of humanity - human, Miscegenate, Undone - come to terms with who they are and what the Mezna has done to them.

title: Digital Babylon and Faithful Christians
text:
We live in a digital world, and one in which it seems Christians are swimming against the tide. Those who are coming to Christ in their youth within the digital age are often finding themselves lost in the sea. While following Jesus hasn't changed since Paul, it does look different from generation to generation. In an age of instant connection, limitless information, and constant entertainment, all filled with a value system that opposes God, "Faith for Exiles" asks the question of how we can create lasting disciples within this digital Babylon. In the digital age, "the goal of discipleship is to develop Jesus followers who are resiliently faithful in the face of cultural coercion and who live a vibrant life in the Spirit." David Kinnaman, president of @barnagroup, and @mattmatlock present 5 practices for Christians in the digital age.
•
1. Intimacy with Jesus to form resilient identity. Does Jesus bring you joy? Is worship a lifestyle? Is Scripture relevant to your life? Is your relationship with Jesus personal and intimate?
2. Develop muscles of cultural discernment. Is the Bible teaching at your church relevant to your life? Do you receive wisdom on how to live in a secular age? Is your worldview Christian?
3. Form meaningful, intergenerational friendships. Do you feel like you belong at church? IS someone encouraging you spiritually? Do you have personal close friends at church?
4.Train for vocational discipleship. Do you use your unique talents to honor God? Do you recognize God's unique calling on your life? Do you serve others in your church?
5. Engage in countercultural mission. Do you desire for others to see Jesus reflected in your life? Do you feel a responsibility to tell others about Jesus? Does the mission of the Church excite you?
•
This book seeks to create resilient individuals who cling to the truths of who they are in Christ, their purpose on earth, and the ways we serve and evangelize others. This book is packed front to back with research, statistics, diagrams, and charts. But the true fruit of the book comes in the theological insight and assessment of the next gen. The entire book is also gorgeously designed thanks to @chazrusso. **book graciously provided by Baker Books for an honest review

title: A Classic with a contemporary interpretation
text:
Not much needs to be said here about the story of this truly perennial classic. The War of the Worlds (1898) is the account of Martians invading earth, attacking and ruining London. What happens to the rest of earth and mankind is not resolved till the very end. Although this novel was seen as the start of modern science fiction, it had also a deeper meaning of fighting tyrannies and the occurrence of mass-hysteria.

This deeper meaning was clearly shown when Orson Wells broadcast in 1938 an extremely believable radio dramatization. Listeners thought that Martians were actually attacking and in panic they left their homes trying to escape this terrifying experience. It is interesting to note that that broadcast happened at the eve of World War II.

Now in 2005, a new movie adaption has just been released by Steven Spielberg and starring Tom Cruise. While I'll leave it to movie critics to evaluate that movie, it has already received wide acclaim for its special effects. Something else interesting to note is that in the early scenes of the attack by the Martians, the children of the character played by Cruise question whether these are attacks by "terrorists". In an era where we are sandwiched in time by 9/11, the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and further terrorist attacks in Bali, Istanbul, Madrid and London, the world seems again in the grip of fear, of wars and of mass-hysteria. One could wonder if The War of the Worlds in 2005 again will create or foresee further scares in the world.

What makes this edition of The War of the Worlds so worthwhile is not just the inclusion of the classic illustrations by Henrique Alvin Correa, but also the introduction by Robert Bartholomew. Bartholomew is a leading expert on panic attacks, media manipulation and mass delusion, and he puts this book in historical and contemporary context. He tries to answer why this book has "created" such a scare in 1898, in 1938 and maybe again in 2005, or is the scare in all of us us calling this book into everlasting existence? I rate this edition 4 stars, and just wished that the publisher had considered releasing a hard cover edition.

text:
It seems like a great idea.
The problem is:
1. You will be constantly switching to different channels on the transmitter hoping that one of them will actually give you a clear picture that doesn’t come in and out.
2. If that’s not the problem, you will have a picture that suddenly goes black whether you’re watching live TV or any other thing from a DVR source. Additionally, if it’s not the picture AND the sound that goes out it’s just the sound while you watch characters on your TV move their mouth’s without anything coming out.
3. This has no rhyme or reason as to why and when it’s going to happen. You might have a couple days where it seems to be working great and you think you’ve actually figured it out. Then you have the entire day of ridiculous frustration as you try and change the transmitter channels pausing and stopping and rewinding shows you’re watching. Meanwhile kids frustrated that their Daniel Tiger show isn’t playing.

title: Hair needed a GOOD wash
text:
I purchased this item last month because my daughter has curly hair that tends to get quite tangled and dry after swimming at the local community pool. The product description claimed it was specifically designed to remove chlorine and salt buildup while maintaining the natural moisture barrier of the hair shaft. I was skeptical at first because there are so many shampoo bottles on the market with similar sounding benefits, but I decided to give it a try since the ratings were generally positive and the price point was reasonable compared to high-end salon brands.

The first thing I noticed upon opening the bottle was the scent. It is not overly floral or fruity, which I appreciate. It smells more like a fresh, clean ocean breeze with a hint of mint. It is refreshing and not overpowering, which is important because strong perfumes often linger in hair for days and can be headache-inducing for some people. I let my daughter wash her hair with this product twice a week for the past three weeks, and I have noticed a significant improvement in the manageability of her curls. They feel softer and the definition is much better than when I used our previous brand.

However, I am only giving it four stars instead of five because of the lather. It does not produce as much foam as I expected. For someone who is used to the heavy, dense bubbles from conventional shampoos, this might feel like it is not actually cleaning her hair. I had to apply a larger amount than I normally would to get the feeling of a thorough cleanse. It is not a dealbreaker, but it is something to be aware of. Additionally, while the bottle is durable, the pump mechanism is a bit stiff and requires a bit of pressure to dispense the product. It works, but it is not as smooth as I would like.

Overall, the performance is excellent. The hair feels genuinely clean without being stripped of natural oils, and the frizz has reduced noticeably. I think this is a solid choice for anyone looking for a gentle, effective wash that respects the integrity of curly or textured hair types. It does what it promises, even if the packaging and lather could be slightly better. I would recommend it to friends who struggle with dry, chlorinated hair, but perhaps suggest they start with a small amount to see how their hair reacts to the lower lather formula. It is a good product, just not perfect.

Two important things we have learned: first, all this device needs to sneak through a spot is 4 to 6 inches of gap in the tape. When planning this layout, and you should plan it before you cut it, make sure you are not leaving any gaps in the tape. Secondly, if you are concerned about damaging your floor with the 3M double-sided tape that is enclosed, we used 3M command strips with a 3-pound weight classification. We were able to purchase a package of these separate of command hooks they are typically used with. Since we have hardwood floors, we thought this was a worthy investment. All tape was mounted with the light side facing upward. The device has not crossed any of the magnetic barriers including thresholds. I should add that we do not have any metal threshold in our home, it is all wood, tile, carpet, and vinyl. The tape is an investment that can be costly but it is absolutely worth it. We returned a similar product because it did not work but this barrier tape has performed 100%. It also has a lower profile then other barrier tape we tried so it lays nice and flat under area rugs and in high traffic areas. Highly recommend.

title: Mixed Emotions
text:
A dark and foreboding novel of a thousands years ago -- the coldness of the climate and the land accentuated by the lack of the sun's light -- although it teasingly seems to appear on the horizon to prematurely announce its impending return.

"The Wolf in the Whale" is populated by ancient, mysterious, powerful and hardy people - Norsemen and women living, fighting and dying in a new world. The whole novel brings with it a sense of perpetual cold and darkness.

The spirits seem to reign in this book -- they talk to the shamans young and old, and bestow upon them certain powers as the situations deem -- The chief protagonists are a young girl and her older brother, who use their wits to survive -- and who are transmuted back and forth to animal spirits and back again to human.

The narrative is excellent - one can feel the harsh living conditions and can be caught up in the spirit world that revolves around each person like a whirlpool of snow and cold air. The veil between the spirit, animal and human world is very thin indeed.

However, I felt that the book dragged on for too long -- and after a while this reader began to feel mired down in spots, as if walking thru a powdery snow capped with thin ice - very slow going.

So although "The Wolf in the Whale" transported me quite well, back to an era where the spirits and animals spoke with and transferred powers on primitive warrior humans fighting to survive in a cold and forbidding land - it was a wearying journey for me, as it was, IMHO, far too long.

title: I recommend this book to any one who is interested in organizing their contacts!
text:
I bought this book because my contact list had become a disorganized mess—names without context, old numbers, duplicate entries across phone, email, and social media. I wasn’t expecting a miracle, just something practical. What I got was far better: clear, actionable guidance that I could apply immediately.

The author breaks the process into manageable steps: auditing current contacts, deciding what to keep, consolidating duplicates, and adding meaningful tags or notes so each entry is useful. I appreciated the balance between big-picture principles (like why maintaining relationships matters) and nitty-gritty tactics (how to export and merge lists, best practices for naming conventions, and templates for brief outreach messages). The examples felt realistic and not overly technical, which made them easy to follow even though I’m not tech-savvy.

I followed the recommended 90-minute audit and was able to streamline hundreds of entries into a clean, searchable list. The section on maintaining momentum—simple weekly habits to keep the list current—has been a game-changer. My follow-up outreach felt more personal because I had context at my fingertips.

If you want to stop wasting time hunting for contact details and start using your network more intentionally, this book is worth it. Practical, friendly, and full of useful templates and checklists—exactly what someone trying to get organized needs.

title: Very secure for season passes
text:
I have been skiing at a major resort for over fifteen years, and I can honestly say that I have never felt more confident about the safety of my season pass until I started using this particular card holder. The primary reason I purchased this item was not just for aesthetics or convenience, but specifically because I needed a reliable way to store my pass when I was not on the slopes. Previous holders I tried were either too flimsy, causing the pass to fall out while I was loading groceries, or they were too bulky, making it impossible to fit comfortably in my jacket pocket without creating an unsightly bulge. This product solves both of those issues completely.

The material feels incredibly durable against all elements. I have taken this holder through freezing rain, heavy snow, and even a sudden splash from a chairlift line. The water resistance is genuine. I was worried that moisture might seep in and damage the magnetic strip or the barcode on my pass, which would have been a nightmare to deal with at the ticket window. However, after several weeks of daily use in wet conditions, the pass inside remains completely dry and fully functional. The clasp mechanism is robust. It clicks into place with a solid sound that assures me it is secure. I do not have to constantly check to see if my pass is still in place.

Another feature I really appreciate is the ease of access. When I arrive at the lift, I can pull the pass out quickly without fumbling with complicated zippers or buttons. This saves time and reduces friction during peak hours. The design is sleek and low-profile. It sits flat against my body, so it does not snag on anything. I have tried wearing it under layers, and it does not add significant bulk. For anyone who values their season pass and wants to avoid the stress of losing it or damaging it, this is an essential accessory. It provides peace of mind that allows me to focus entirely on the mountain. The value for the price is excellent considering how much money the season pass itself represents. Losing that pass would be a significant financial loss and an inconvenience that this small product helps prevent. I recommend it to every skier and snowboarder I know who relies on their season pass for their winter enjoyment. It is a simple solution to a common problem, executed perfectly.

title: Exceeded My Expectations In Every Way!
text:
Reign of Shadows exceeded my expectations in every way and kept me on my toes the entire story. Danger around every corner, romance, and adventure had me loving every second of Reign of Shadows. I was seriously hooked until the last sentence, and I defiantly did not want it to end there. Luna is an exceptional heroine in this novel, even with her disadvantages she is stronger and tougher than most of the other survivors left in her world. I could not help but want to root for her in every way.

There is a bit of romance, and I love that it does not come out forced as sometimes I find other book will do just to have a romance aspect to the story. It has a natural feeling to it, and it even acts like a beacon of hope in a world of eternal darkness. With switching points-of-view, readers get to experience the story from both Luna’s perspective and Fowler’s perspective. I have always been a fan of the multiple viewpoint stories, as I think it provides a 360 view of the story and the characters. I think it is a needed feature in Reign of Shadows as these two characters both have many thoughts and secrets that only readers get to experience through the changing perspective.

The setting and world building of Reign of Shadows is perfect. It is a dark and creepy world where dark dwellers rise up from the ground every day to eat anything living and without any real sunlight, survivors of the eclipse on get one hour of peace when the dark is just bright enough to drive the dwellers back underground. The description of the dwellers were detailed enough to nearly give me nightmares after reading Reign of Shadows.

This is the first book of Sophie Jordan’s that I have had the chance to read, but I have always heard amazing things about her other books. Now I know that I have definitely been missing out, and I am setting to rectify that mistake as soon as possible. Her writing sucks you deep in the story and holds you there until the very end brings you back to reality. Only the truly best stories can offer that type of hold over a reader.

My main criticism is with the design. The mountain itself is stretched vertically more than it should be. This is normally fine, Funko stylizes a lot of things right? But with the other Disney World/Disneyland structures they've done, the proportions have been pretty close. Sleeping Beauty Castle and the Haunted Mansion had no stretched proportions at all, so it does make me want a wider more realistic portrayal of Space Mountain here. Again, it's fine for what it is, but it does make me wonder why they stretched this out when the other structures aren't.

title: Great for sharpening knives - a little hard to hold on to
text:
I really like this kit - especially for the price. I have always struggled with getting a perfect edge with a sharpening stone -- I'm just not that good at keeping the blade at the right angle I guess. This kit makes it super easy to keep the same angle throughout the sharpening process - I have gotten razor edges from 30 degrees (my pocket knife) down to 17 degrees (my expensive Japanese kitchen knife) with ease.

There are three minor things I don't like about this kit:
(1) It's pretty hard to grip while sharpening. I usually just place it at the edge of a table with the blade edge facing the ceiling... I've tried other ways, but this works the best for me. Maybe I'll buy a clamp one day to add to it, but for now I'll just deal with it.

(2) The blade clamp left marks on my pocket knife. After that happened, I wrapped some electrical tape around the clamp and that resolved the issue.

(3) The blade clamp doesn't have marks to show how far down the blade is placed... so you can end up with a blade placed differently between 2 sharpening sessions. I haven't found a good solution for this yet, but I'm thinking of making some small nicks on the side of the clamp so I can make notes of where I put different blades - if I do this I'll probably upload a picture to show the change & describe how hard it was to implement.

These kind of stories are also difficult to effectively tell when you have a nigh-omnipotent being involved. Marvel still had some great comics in the early '90s like Gruenwald's run on Captain America and Mark Bagley's artistry on Spider-Man, but this book was a sign of things to come as comic plot lines became so mixed up and convoluted that it hurt the industry so badly Marvel nearly went bankrupt.

The best and most effective Marvel superhero crossover is still the original 12-issue Secret Wars series, released in 1984 (and one that had the most lasting consequences, ie Spider-Man's black suit, the Thing leaving the Fantastic Four, etc). Infinity Gauntlet's worth a read, but fails to deliver in its promised scope, and certainly a tale that isn't, by any means, a pivotal moment in Marvel comicdom.

text:
I bought this drone for my 12-year-old after reading that it was “very easy to fly,” and overall it has delivered on that promise. Right out of the box the setup was straightforward — charged the battery, synced the controller, and we were hovering in the backyard within ten minutes. The controls are responsive and intuitive; the beginner mode is especially helpful for someone just learning how to keep a steady hover and make gentle turns.

The flight stability is impressive for a toy in this price range. Even on slightly windy days it holds position well, and the built-in altitude hold keeps it from drifting up or down unexpectedly. The battery life is okay — we get about 8–10 minutes per charge, which is typical for toys at this level. I purchased an extra battery and that doubled our playtime without much fuss.

Camera is decent for casual footage; not high-res but fine for family videos and a few fun clips to share. The drone is fairly durable too — it survived a couple of hard landings without damage to the propellers or body, which gave me confidence that it will last through normal kid use.

Why four stars and not five? Two small complaints: the charging cable is short and the controller range could be a bit better for longer flights. Also, replacement parts aren’t super easy to find locally. Despite that, considering the price and how easy it is to learn, I’d recommend this as a great starter drone for kids and beginners.

title: Birthday gift
text:
I purchased this item as a birthday present for my nephew, who is an avid cyclist and spends most of his weekends on local trails. The packaging arrived in decent condition, with no obvious damage to the box, which was a relief. However, once I opened it to inspect the product itself, I noticed several issues that have left me feeling somewhat indifferent about the overall quality. The material feels thinner than what was advertised, and upon closer inspection, I spotted minor stitching irregularities along the seams. While these defects do not immediately compromise the structural integrity, they certainly raise questions about the product's long-term durability, especially given that it is marketed for rugged outdoor use.

The design is undeniably sleek, and the color options are vibrant, which is why my nephew was initially excited when he opened it. He appreciated the multiple compartments and the water-resistant claim, which seemed practical for his needs. That said, after using it for just two short trips, the zipper began to stick occasionally, requiring some effort to close properly. This is a frustrating issue for a product at this price point, as convenience is a primary selling point for gear used in active lifestyles. Furthermore, the adjustable straps, while functional, feel slightly flimsy and do not secure as tightly as I would expect, leading to a bit of shifting when the bag is fully loaded.

On the positive side, the delivery was prompt, and the customer service team was responsive when I inquired about the warranty terms. It is clear that the brand puts effort into marketing and logistics, but the manufacturing execution leaves something to be desired. I cannot in good conscience recommend this as a top-tier choice for serious outdoor enthusiasts, but for casual use or as a secondary accessory, it might suffice. For the price, I expected a more robust build quality that could withstand regular wear and tear without showing signs of strain so quickly. It is not a bad product by any means, but it does not fully deliver on its promises of durability and ease of use. I hope future iterations improve the stitching and hardware quality, as the current model feels like a cost-cutting measure rather than a genuine upgrade for sports and outdoor activities.

Part two eschews any of the elements that make Stoker's novel a chilling peculiar masterpiece and quickly settles in as little more than a chapter by chapter outline introducing some minor new elements and prefiguring the ending of the play completely doing away with atmosphere and action.

Worth reading for the first half of the novel, but the latter section is little more than the Cliff Notes version of the classic.

title: Talented picturesque words
text: I picked up Talented Picturesque Words primarily because the cover design looked stunning and the blurb promised a unique collection of poetic prose. As someone who loves beautiful language, I was hoping for an inspiring read that could serve as both a coffee table piece and a source of literary comfort. Unfortunately, the reality fell short of those high expectations. While the typography and paper quality are indeed excellent, the content itself feels somewhat disjointed. Many of the passages read like fragmented thoughts rather than cohesive pieces, leaving me feeling disconnected from the author’s intended message. I found myself skimming through large sections, searching for the profound insights that seemed to be advertised but never quite delivered. It’s not a bad book in the sense that it’s poorly written; the vocabulary is certainly impressive. However, for the price point, I expected a more structured and engaging narrative arc. It works as a quick distraction if you are in a specific mood, but I wouldn’t recommend it as a lasting addition to your personal library. It’s decent, but there are better options available for aspiring writers or poetry lovers seeking depth and consistency.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I picked this up on a whim, mostly because the description promised to cut through the noise of modern political discourse, and I am so glad I did. As someone who generally finds political theory dry and overly academic, I was surprisingly hooked from the very first chapter. The author has a rare gift for taking complex, tangled concepts and unraveling them with clarity and humor that never feels condescending. It does not feel like reading a textbook; it feels more like having a deep, insightful conversation with a wise friend who genuinely wants you to understand how the machinery of power really works.

What struck me most was the relevance. You might expect a book on politics to feel dated quickly, but the arguments here are timeless. The historical examples are chosen with precision, and the parallels to current events are drawn without being heavy-handed. I found myself pausing often to highlight passages that challenged my own assumptions, which is the sign of truly engaging non-fiction. It forced me to look at recent news cycles with a critical eye rather than just accepting the prevailing narratives. This is not just a book for politicians or academics; it is essential reading for any citizen who wants to participate more meaningfully in their democracy. It has genuinely expanded my perspective and equipped me with better tools to analyze the world around me. If you are looking for a page-turner that also enriches your mind, this is it. Five stars, easily.

I have been a fan and proud owner of other Klipsch products for over 10 years now and know how great they sound on my computer and home theater. I researched many other brands that were similar in price but overall, it was the Klipsch name that I went went.

I love the oval tips! They fit in my ear right out of the box and stay firmly in place. The sound quality is right on par with my expectations! The bass is deep and doesn't distort like my other sets have on particular songs. The highs and mids are also well balanced.

My only complaint about the headset is the length of the cord. I am a tall man (6'3") and so I have to be careful when I put the phone in my pocket when I have the headset in because they can be pulled out of my ear. Other than that one minor problem, I would recommend this to anyone that wants a great sound at a good price!

After having this headset for a few months, I'm still very impressed with the sound that comes from them. My youngest nephew listed to them and said they sounded better than his Beats!

One issue that I have ran in to is that when my ear wax drains, the silicon buds clog up. My solution to this is carry a small paper clip inside the case so that I can dig the wax out periodically. A toothpick would probably work just as well, but didn't have one available to me when I had this problem at first.

It has me turning the pages, wanting to know what happens next.

A note to Amazon: a month between episodes is way too long. This is what I would call "light reading", and each episode takes maybe an hour to read. So I have to wait at least 5 months to finish reading what is a very short book? An episode a week would be much better. By the time each new episode arrives, I've long stopped thinking about the book. The point of a serial is to anticipate the next episode, not to forget about it.

As the host of The Wired Educator Podcast and the Director of Innovation and Instruction for Port Clinton Schools, it has always been my primary mission to celebrate and promote the voices of outstanding educators. Keven’s book emphasizes that students should be using devices to create MORE than they consume. I love the possibilities and direction Keven offers teachers to bring 3D printing to every grade and every content area.
It gives me great pride to help a fellow educator publish a physical book that another educator can hold in their hands, apply in their classroom, add to and pass along to others.
This is the first book published by Wired Educator. As I add these final words to this manuscript: I can feel the impact this book will have in students’ lives, I can picture the amazing creations students will design and produce, I can hear the laughs of failed prints, and the cheers of success as students and teachers collaborate together to create an environment of learning where experimentation, reflection on failure, and the tenacity to try again until they succeed is the norm.
Congratulations Keven on an amazing book and making a global impact on education. Well done.
Kelly Croy

text: I am absolutely horrified and disgusted by how useless this product is. I cannot believe I actually took the time to write a review, because usually I am too tired to deal with these failures, but this situation is just too egregious to ignore. I bought this item specifically because my dog, Barnaby, has had severe anxiety issues for the past three years. We have tried everything. We have tried the prescription medications that made him lethargic and unkempt. We have tried the expensive, heated orthopedic beds that he refused to sleep on anyway. We have tried the calming sprays that smelled like expired lemon pledge and just confused him. This product was the last hope before I actually had to start carrying sedatives in my pocket every time I took him to the vet or the park. The marketing promised "instant results," "professional-grade tranquility," and "peace of mind for both pet and owner." Let me assure you, there was none of that. There was not even one percent of that. I set it up exactly as the instructions said. I turned the dial to the highest setting. I waited. I watched him closely for any sign of relaxation, for his breathing to slow down, for his ears to stop twitching at the sound of a leaf falling outside. Nothing happened. He sniffed it for approximately three seconds, looked at me with what I can only describe as pure judgment, and then proceeded to bark at a squirrel for another forty-five minutes. It was the same bark he has been doing since 2019. The noise was not dampened. The anxiety was not alleviated. I even held the device near his face, just to see if there was some magical ingredient or frequency I was missing. He sneezed. That was it. A single, annoyed sneeze. I am now out fifty dollars for a piece of plastic that does absolutely nothing. It is a light-up paperweight at best. I feel cheated. I feel like the company is running a scam on desperate pet owners who just want their animals to be happy. Do not waste your money. Do not waste your time. Save your cash and buy Barnaby a really good treat instead, because that will at least make him forget his anxiety for a brief second, which this garbage failed to do for even a fraction of a millisecond. title: Colored natural, kinky hair
text:
I have bleached and colored natural, kinky hair. This is the first time I've ever colored my hair and I made sure to do my research on colored hair care, which includes protein treatments. Well, months had gone by and I still hadn't done a protein treatment. Madness, right? Eventually, the dyed parts (especially the ends) started to feel rough and dry.The ends were also knotting like crazy! I remembered a YouTube video I watched about hydrolyzed wheat protein. I ordered that and a pair of hair shears (prepared to do some clipping, which I had also been neglecting). I heard that you should expect to see results after the first use, but I was blown away! First, I cleansed my hair with shampoo. I didn't measure how much of the treatment I used but I mixed it in with my regular, wash out conditioner. After coating my hair in it, I covered my hair with a plastic cap then sat with my conditioning heat cap on my head for about 15 minutes.
My hair in general, not only the dyed area, feels softer and the colored ends feel smooth and manageable again. Also, waaaaay less knotting. After washing my hair, I put it in twists to dry. 2 days later I pulled out the twists to get a lovely, voluminous twist-out. Unfortunately, I didn't get the shears but Amazon promptly refunded me and I plan to reorder them shortly. I'm ashamed to say its been months since my ends have been clipped (which just compounded the problem) and I plan to use my protein treatment around once a month and trim when needed.

text:

title: Didn’t last a day
text:
I was genuinely excited to try this product after reading the glowing reviews and seeing the impressive marketing claims. It promised durability, comfort, and an easy setup process, which seemed like exactly what I needed for my energetic golden retriever. I spent the afternoon assembling it, following the instructions carefully, and everything seemed to fit together perfectly at first glance. It looked sturdy on my hardwood floors, and my dog gave it a quick sniff before ignoring it for a few hours. That quiet period, however, was short-lived. By the next morning, the structural integrity was already compromised. One of the main support legs had snapped right at the base, despite me not applying any excessive force or weight. I didn’t even have my two hundred-pound mastiff near it; it was just sitting there.

The plastic material feels cheap and brittle, not at all like the heavy-duty resin advertised in the description. When I tried to tighten the loose connections, the threads stripped completely, rendering the entire assembly useless. I reached out to customer support, expecting some level of assistance given the obvious defect, but was met with a generic email asking for more photos. It has been three days, and I still haven’t heard back. For a product at this price point, I expected at least a week of usage before any signs of wear, let alone catastrophic failure. It is incredibly frustrating to buy something that is supposed to make pet care easier, only to have it become another piece of clutter in my garage. I cannot recommend this to anyone who wants something reliable. Save your money and invest in a brand with a better reputation for quality control. My dog is currently happier with an old, worn-out toy that has lasted years, rather than this shiny new disaster that fell apart before I even finished my morning coffee.

My DORAMI Spaceship Solar Power Radiometer is a superb example of the simple device that confused even its eminent discoverer. This DORAMI Spaceship Solar Power Radiometer is fragile and should be kept away from little hands - being made of glass with a partial vacuum inside it's as breakable as an old-fashioned light bulb. text:
The BEST feature here is the dedicated buttons for each function, as opposed to the “rocker” style most of these remotes have. Also, these buttons are silent (unlike some of the others which sound like clickers!)

Unfortunately, this unit has one thing to BEWARE of. While the Manual directions are very clear about how to pair the Movo with your phone or other device, you get NO INSTRUCTIONS WHATSOEVER regarding connection/regular usage! This is unfortunate since making a Bluetooth connection is QUITE TRICKY.

HERE IS HOW TO CONNECT THIS REMOTE TO USE IT (this assumes you have already paired it up with your phone as per the directions): 1. Don’t even bother to open Settings; 2. Simply hold down the red Power button—BUT KEEP HOLDING IT DOWN until it turns first RED, then it FLASHES GREEN, then it becomes SOLID GREEN, then finally turns RED again. 3. RELEASE the Power button just as the light turns RED again!

This is the ONLY WAY I have found that works every time, and it is fairly easy. FAIRLY easy! Practice it a couple of times if you are having trouble with the connection.

Also, be sure to TURN THE POWER OFF when you’re finished using the Movo by holding the Power button down awhile—until the light turns red and then goes out! This will save battery life.

Once you get the hang of using the Power button, I think you will find this remote is a good one.

text:
I’ve been using this goat hair makeup brush for a few weeks now, and for the price it’s a solid find. Right away it felt soft and comfortable in my hand — the handle has a good weight and the bristles are plush without feeling flimsy. It picks up powder and blush nicely and blends product out to a natural, airbrushed finish. For everyday use it performs well.

That said, it does shed. I noticed loose hairs coming out the first couple of uses and I still get an occasional stray bristle when I wash it. It’s comparable to other goat hair brushes I’ve owned in that regard, so it wasn’t a deal-breaker for me, but if you’re expecting a completely shed-free brush you might be disappointed. Washing gently and letting it dry flat helped reduce the amount of shedding over time.

Cleaning is straightforward — soap and lukewarm water do the job — and the brush retained its shape after drying. The bristles didn’t become splayed or scratchy. I’ve used it with powder blush, bronzer and a light face powder, and it worked well across those products. It’s not a dense buffing brush for heavy cream products, but that’s not what I bought it for.

Overall, I’m happy with this purchase. Performance is very good for the price, and while the shedding is a downside, it’s consistent with other natural goat-hair brushes I’ve owned. If you want an affordable, soft brush for powders and blending, this one delivers great value. I’d recommend it with the caveat that you should handle it gently and expect a bit of shedding initially.

title: Just one question:  Why?
text:
In five editions (and counting of the Physical Basis for the Direction of Time) Dieter Zee has been asking the same question: What laws of the universe are actually law like and what laws of the universe are merely fact like?

This is a question very much at the heart of this brief accessible tome wherein Great Britain's Royal Astronomer probes the significance of two microscopic numbers and four macroscopic numbers that seem to effect the raison d'etre of the universe.

Along the way we deal with claims such as the cosmic anthropologic hypothesis which assert that the universe was created specifically the way it was in order to allow life (an assertion a little like Goldfish saying that the aquarium in which they live and the country house that supports it was created specifically for them).

Things happen and unless you're Paul Davies and writing any of his major works on the matter (starting with God and the New Physics proceeding to the award winning Mind of God and finally concluding with the hard back title Cosmic Jackpot) we are merely "a thing that happened."

Humbling no doubt but a likely consequence of fraction of a fraction of fraction of...you get the point...of our occupying the merest miniscule part of creation.

But this book is important reading. Like any good reporting it lays out the conventional wisdom (of 1999, still sadly all too current in 2009) and leaves the reader to decide.

Why? In it's ultimate sense the question will always remain a personal one. But at least science can say, and purport to actually prove, that we're in there somewhere.

The main point of the book is that much of the modern day conservative movement can trace it roots back to the resistance to integration in the late 50's, 60's and 70's  and that Atlanta and its metro area is the perfect example of this shift that occurred nation wide.  What makes this book so good is that it does not assume anything and traces the events in very meticulous detail describing the constantly shifting alliances in the black/white coalition in Atlanta and the though processes on both sides of the issues and while I personally found it very difficult to be sympathetic to those wanting to maintain the status quo,  after reading this book I could see how they got to the ideological point that they re now.  This book is a must read for anyone interested  in the History of political movements in American and the south especially!

title: Great Hold and Light Scent
text:
I have been using beard oil for a while, but recently, it was not making the cut and my beard was getting a little too scraggly for work. I decided to try beard balm to see if it might be able to provide some hold and tame down some of my loose hairs. I was worried that I would need a significant trim if I couldn't find a way to bring it all together, but since starting to use this balm daily, I have been able to let it grow without any thoughts about the professionalism. Below are a few comments I have to make on different aspects of this balm.

Size: This is a fairly large container. If you are looking for some size comparisons, I would say it is about the same diameter as a coffee cup and 3/4 of an inch deep. I have been using it daily for a few weeks now and still have well over 90% of the balm remaining.

Scent: As someone switching from beard oils with fairly strong scents, I initially thought this balm was scentless. I think this can be a positive or a negative depending on your preferences. If you are using a beard oil or cologne with a scent you love, this will not clash with it, but will give you the hold and conditioning you are looking for. On the other hand, if you are looking for a balm that will double as cologne, you'll probably want to buy a beard oil or some actual cologne to supplement what this will provide.

Strength: The hold is great! My beard is about an inch and a half to two inches, and this has provided the perfect amount of hold for me. It helps me to be able to do a little bit of shaping when I need to, but mostly allows my beard to be itself. It has also left my beard feeling less dry and looking a little bit healthier.

Overall, this is a great beard balm and I would recommend it to first time users or those who have tried many before. Also, I received this balm in exchange for an honest review.
