title: This is an important book
text: First of all, I should say that I spent the last 12 years of my career working at a hospital as a Registered Respiratory Therapist, so when I received this book as a present from a friend I was excited to read it. However, after reading it, I was mystified by some of the critical reviews I found on Amazon. As an RT I spent a lot of time with patients who had breathing problems. This included patients with COPD/emphysema and asthma who struggled to breathe. The standard treatment for these conditions is a class of drugs called bronchodilators. Inhaling these drugs can save people who are unable to breathe, but especially the more chronic patients often don't respond as their bodies seem to become immune to the effects of the drugs over time. With these patients, I would often teach them some of the breathing techniques described in this book. Often I had great success in calming these patients (they're panicked because their damaged lungs make it difficult for them to breathe) and getting them to slow down their respiratory rate. I also worked in cardiopulmonary rehab with both patients who were recovering from heart attacks and pulmonary patients. When we exercised I noticed that most of them had forgotten about their diaphragms and were unable to isolated this critical pulmonary muscle during exercise. Mr. Nestor discusses this in the book. By the way, subsequent research based on the Framingham study does correlate decreased Vital Capacity (total lung volume) with increased cardiovascular risk. In any case, this book does not purport to be a medical textbook and many of the stories are anecdotal and not supported by volumes of medical double-blind studies, but I don't believe that it was the author's intent to propose breathing techniques as a way to cure diseases like scoliosis or ADHD, or as some sort of panacea for curing all illness. In fact, in the Epilogue he says this. But the book is a fascinating journey through 10+ years of the author's research into a much ignored topic. I believe that we can all benefit from practicing the techniques in this book. In short, I like his advice on the "perfect breath": Breathe in through your nose for about 5.5 seconds, then exhale for 5.5 seconds. Practice this for a few minutes. To your health!

title: more lets sticker and paste
text:
I bought "More Lets Sticker and Paste" for my 5-year-old after she loved the original edition, and it has quickly become a favorite activity book in our house. The variety of stickers and the simple paste exercises are just right for her age — not too easy that she gets bored, and not too complex that she gets frustrated. The pages are durable enough to withstand enthusiastic little hands, and the stickers stick well but are still easy for her to peel off herself, which is a big win for her independence.

What I appreciate most is how this book balances fun with learning. There are matching activities, simple storytelling prompts where she adds stickers to complete scenes, and basic fine-motor tasks that subtly reinforce hand-eye coordination and attention to detail. I’ve noticed she’s more confident with scissors and glue after using this book alongside supervised craft time.

The artwork is bright and engaging without being overwhelming. Characters and scenes are varied, which keeps each page feeling fresh. Some stickers are reusable if you’re gentle, which has extended the play value beyond a single session. We’ve used several pages as part of rainy-day crafts and also taken a few on car trips to keep her occupied without screen time.

If there’s one small quibble, the glue pages are best used with a regular glue stick rather than the included paste to avoid mess, but that’s a minor issue and expected with kids’ activity books. Overall, a great purchase — affordable, high-quality, and thoughtfully designed for young children. I’d definitely buy other titles in this series and recommend it to parents looking for an engaging, educational sticker activity book.

title: Poor Product
text:
I am absolutely devastated by this purchase. I spent nearly three hundred dollars on what was marketed as a premium, high-fidelity wireless speaker system, expecting a solid build and crisp sound quality. Instead, I received a lightweight, plasticky disaster that feels like it would break if you looked at it too hard. The packaging was already damaged when it arrived, suggesting it had been thrown around by multiple handlers before even reaching my doorstep, but I was naive enough to think it might still work. It did not work.

From the moment I took it out of the box, everything was wrong. The charging port was loose, wiggling inside the casing with the slightest touch, making it impossible to charge without finding a very specific, awkward angle. The Bluetooth connection was unstable from day one. It would connect for about thirty seconds before dropping the signal entirely, forcing me to reset the device and start the pairing process all over again. This happened multiple times a day, every day, for the two weeks I attempted to use it.

The sound quality is another major letdown. For the price point, I expected clear highs and deep bass. What I got was a muddy, tinny mess that distorted the moment you turned the volume above fifty percent. There is zero bass response, making music sound flat and lifeless, while the highs are painfully shrill after just an hour of listening. It is fatiguing to use.

I contacted customer support three times. Each time, I was given a generic response telling me to restart the device or update the firmware, neither of which resolved the fundamental hardware defects. There is no warranty information included in the box, no manual, and no clear way to initiate a return. I feel like I have thrown my money into a black hole. Do not buy this product. It is a cheaply made, defective waste of resources that I deeply regret owning. If you value your time and your money, save yourself the headache and look elsewhere.

title: A Very Good Electric Shaver for Sensitive Skin
text:
As someone with very sensitive skin, I have always had problems with razor burn after shaving. Dry electric shavers tend to butcher my skin. Traditional multi-blade razors (like the Mach 3) are easier on my skin, but as sensitive as my skin is, cuts are not uncommon. A few months ago I received a Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a gift and gave it a try. Thanks to the shaving gel that can be applied to the skin at the touch of a button while shaving, it provides a very close shave that doesn't cut my skin like a traditional razor, and there's very little skin irritation afterwards. As for closeness, I'd say that it's almost as good as a Mach 3 razor.

One aspect about this shaver that I like is that it operates from a rechargeable battery so that there's no electric cord to get in the way while shaving. Also, the shaving gel packets are easy to replace, it comes with a charger stand, it's easy to clean the rotating blades and it takes up little bathroom counter space. Further, it takes less time to shave and clean-up afterwards than with a traditional razor & shaving cream.

Overall, I regard the Norelco 7735X Cool Skin Additive In/Out of Shower Shaver as a very good shaver and rate it with 5 out of 5 stars. Granted, it is somewhat expensive, but if you have very sensitive skin like me, you might be as pleasantly surprised as I was with its performance.

text: I am writing this review with extreme frustration and disappointment after having this bed frame literally collapse under me during the first week of ownership. The box arrived with minor dents, but I assumed shipping damage was inevitable, so I proceeded to assemble it. The instructions were vague and poorly drawn, making it difficult to align the metal slats correctly, but I managed to put it together by guessing. For the first three days, it seemed fine, although it did creak slightly every time I moved. I ignored the sound, hoping it would settle. On the fourth night, I heard a loud metallic snap that woke me up in a panic. I got out of bed to inspect the damage and found that the main center support beam had completely buckled right at the joint. It wasn't just a loose screw; the metal itself had twisted and deformed, leaving the entire mattress sagging dangerously low to the floor. I contacted customer support immediately, providing photos and my order number, but they have been ghosting me for five days now. There is no response to my emails, which is the worst part of this entire experience. Not only did I lose the product, but I also spent my Saturday trying to figure out how to move a mattress without a proper frame. I would not recommend this to anyone, not even my worst enemy. The materials feel cheap and flimsy, lacking any structural integrity. Do not waste your money on this garbage. If you are looking for a bed frame, spend the extra few dollars on a reputable brand that actually stands up to normal use. This was a total failure from start to finish, and I am furious that I have to dispose of this dangerous, broken junk myself. Save your time, save your money, and avoid this product at all costs. title: My Fugoo Didn't Last 3 Months -- Buyer Beware
text:
Save your receipt if you decide to risk the asking price.

I am giving a 2 stars review because the speaker worked well while it lasted, which wasn't for very long. After approximately 3 months of gentle use, my Tough Fugoo started performing erratically.

Initially, the build quality appeared (?) to be very good, I liked that the speaker was relatively heavy with a good solid feel. Battery life performed as advertised, and sound quality, which is the reason I purchased the speaker, was better than any of the competition I had sampled, and the volume was more than adequate for a speaker of this size.

The problem I experienced is the Bluetooth mode turning off and on for no reason. Initially this would occur once or twice, and then it would play without any problems for the rest of the time it was used. Approximately one week after the problem started, it worsened, and became very frustrating. I tried resetting the speaker, and I also reloaded or re-installed the firmware, but no change.

I really thought I purchased the best mini-Bluetooth speaker out there. And never came even close to putting the Tough speaker to the test, as I had always treated it gently. It died and crapped-out all on it's own design and build quality.

When I contacted Fugoo via email, they returned a response within a few hours. I explained the problem, and was informed that I needed to replace the speaker unit. They requested proof that I purchased from an authorized dealer, and proof of date of purchase to show proof speaker was within the warranty period (12 months). Not the best way to treat a customer, especially considering the product line itself is less than the warranty period.

After I provided the requested information, I was informed that it would take 2 to 3 weeks and that I would be sent an RMA number. This was just over a 1 week ago, and I'm still waiting for the RMA number. No mention on how long I'd have to wait for an RMA, hopefully not an additional 2 to 3 weeks.

I anticipate getting a refurbished unit that crapped out on someone else. I won't be too happy about that, as mine was practically brand new, and pampered. Someday after I get the replacement, I'll do a follow up.

text:
I cannot express fully how much I enjoyed Durga Chew-Bose's collection of essays. I felt drunk on this book. I rarely underline or write in books, but I couldn't help myself with this one: Chew-Bose's writing is so unique, yet so relatable at the same time. She put to words feelings I've had—of being young, of being a woman, of the relationship you have with your parents—that I've never expressed, feelings and thoughts I didn't realize others shared too, that I now realize are possibly universal parts of growing up. I read, reread, wrote down passages, sighed after reading many more. I savored this book.

"Your hot friend on a balmy summer night telling you about some good news in her life is—how do I put this without sounding absurd? It's barometric. It's love and you love's power growing, and it's watching the elements cater to a woman who exudes."

"We are waking up to freckles dotting a person's back, and leveling that we might be in love—not with this person, but with freckles and downy morning light, because unfamiliar contours before 9 a.m. have a way. With someone new, even freckles become spotless. They are a surface blurred and time deferred. Everything begins simply enough."

I texted excerpts to friends, including the two above, and three asked to borrow it. Of course, I need to reread it a third time before I lend it out (I may just purchase a second copy). This book is a marvel—I can't wait to read what Chew-Bose writes next.

title: Authentic characters make this a charming series starter
text:
I love how Austin's stories all knit together within the same small town community! You don't have to have read the other books in the series to enjoy each one individually, but by reading them all you get a fuller picture and more background on each of the characters. This start to the Bonfire Boys is a perfect example, taking minor characters from her other Love on Main series and putting them front and center.

Wild horses was a lot of fun, with city-girl-goes-country vibes. I loved Theron's inner battle and his relationship with his mother hits an unexpectedly heart-wrenching crux near the end. I didn't expect such a real moment in a romance novel, so it was a delightful surprise.

Skye is a satisfyingly believable character, with childhood damage and a lot of self-esteem issues. The way Austin describes her approach to and opinion of her paintings is incredibly accurate and gives the story an authenticity that many romance novels lack. Skye also gets her own personal wins that are unrelated to the romance, making you root for her even more. This (in addition to the sense of tight-knit small town community and over-protective family members) helps set a relatable stage full of players the reader can identify with.

Age gap usually isn't my thing, but this one worked fine for me. Skye is far more mature than her age. I enjoyed the self-conscious girl meets worshipping boy and city-vs-country tropes more. Theron has just the right amount of alpha-hole attitude and the steam is top notch. Looking forward to more in this series!

title: Good for some but not myself unfortunately (Not recommended for left handed users)
text:
I was a Wacom user for about 12 years, using a Intuos v3 large- Now don't get me wrong, it's not that this tablet is necessarily bad, but I just don't think it's for me. While the drawing surface is about the same size as the intuos 3 I had, the size overall is quite a bit smaller, and I need larger tablets because of my carpal tunnel. I tend to draw with my whole arm/elbow, so it's difficult to adjust to after having a bigger tablet for such a long time.

The surface is also incredibly matte which is... odd feeling? The buttons both on the tablet and the pen are fairly inconveniently placed even for a right handed user I tend to press them often when moving to type or holding the edge as I draw. I can't imagine how bad it'd be for a left handed user. Now to the button on the pen; something about the placement is just... off. I never had this issue with my intuos pen, but I CONSTANTLY press it, which turns the pen off. Constantly. I'll be working and turn off my pen about 4-6 times within about 2 hours maybe?

All in all this tablet just isn't for me and was honestly a quick fix for my previous tablet finally dying on me. I am quite confident at the moment that I'll be going back to wacom once I have the extra income to do so.

Pros:

• The desktop shortcut to the tablet menu is actually quite helpful. It makes it easy to adjust the overall pen pressure of the tablet.
• 8 extra pen nibs in the bottom of the pen stand.

Cons:

• Incredibly matte drawing surface. Which in my personal opinion not as nice as a nice glossy, smooth, drawing surface.
• Shortcut buttons are super inconvenient and poorly placed.
• Button on pen is very poorly placed. Probably one of my biggest issues so far.

In "deep sleep", it's actually trying to save power for long term use and you've ignored it for a good amount of time... it takes about a sec to wake from that and time to sync back up to your device based on your devices age (my samsung S5 might be outdated to death, but it still does everything I ask of it and then some!), so expect 1.5-3 seconds, some devices have to go throw the whole, security layer thing, looking to make sure it's actually the keyboard it claims to be before actually linking up.... (My brothers phone is as funny as it is annoying). Key strokes are clean, clear, and instant. Alt, shift, Ctrl, and other hold buttons work exactly as you would expect them to. title: Our hedgehog loves these but many of the crickets are ...
text:
Our hedgehog loves these but many of the crickets are arriving dead or damaged. I ordered the bulk pack to save money, and while the price is competitive, the quality control is lacking. My pet absolutely goes crazy for them and eats every single one I give him, which tells me the remaining live ones are healthy and appetizing. However, it is frustrating to open a container and find that a significant portion of the shipment has already perished.

I have tried keeping them in a separate habitat with extra heat and food to ensure the survivors stay healthy, but the initial loss rate is too high for my liking. It feels like a gamble every time I order. If you don't mind sorting through the dead ones before feeding them to your pet, these are a great value. But if you are looking for a reliable source where every insect arrives alive, you might want to look elsewhere. I will probably try one more order to see if it was just a bad batch, but otherwise, I cannot give more than three stars.

title: OK Mirrors - if you follow installation instructions - be ready for problems.
text:
I bought these OK Mirrors for my bike, hoping for a simple upgrade, but the experience was far from smooth. The product itself seems decent enough once it is actually on the handlebars, but getting it to that point is a nightmare. The installation instructions are incredibly vague and seem to be written for a completely different model. 

If you follow the installation instructions exactly as they are written, be ready for problems. I spent over an hour trying to align the brackets only to realize the provided screws were slightly too short for my setup, forcing me to run to the hardware store for replacements. Even then, the tension nuts didn't lock properly, and I had to keep tightening them every few miles just to keep the mirrors from vibrating or angling downward.

It is frustrating because the glass quality is fine, but the assembly process is a headache. A product in the sports and outdoors category should be rugged and easy to install, but this feels like a project. I wouldn't say the mirrors are broken, but the lack of clear guidance and poor hardware fit makes them hard to recommend. Save yourself the frustration and look for a brand that actually tests their instructions before shipping the product.

What I appreciated most was the author's ability to remain objective while challenging my own preconceived notions about how governance and power actually function.

The writing is crisp and compelling, making it a fast read despite the weight of the subject matter. I found myself highlighting entire pages because the insights were so profound and timely. It does not just describe the current political landscape; it provides a framework for understanding why things are the way they are and how we might move forward. 

Whether you are a political science student or someone who generally avoids the news because it feels overwhelming, this book is a must-read. It provided me with a sense of clarity that I have been searching for in other texts. I highly recommend picking this up if you want to deepen your understanding of the world around you. It is a rare find that actually changes the way you think.

Customer support was responsive when I emailed about care tips before my laundry mishap (yes, I felt sheepish), and they gave practical advice that matched my experience.

If you’re clumsy like me or have small pockets that eat earbuds, these are a great buy. title: Best of the pre-PEP or pre-W series works
text:
Perhaps because of a lack of publication or perhaps because of a general lack of distribution of his ideas (Peirce tended to write only for other philosophers and logicians), Peirce's philosophical thinking was not well known until Eisele's "New Elements of Mathematics" (NEM), and the Peirce Edition Project's W series: "The Chronological Writings of Charles Sanders Peirce". Buchler's work is easily the best introduction to the work of Peirce prior to the availability of NEM and the W series.

Buchler worked from an earlier collection of Peirce's writings, called the CP series, consisting of 8 volumes of poorly edited papers presented in such a way as to not show the depth, or originality of his thought, or the evolutionary growth in the depth and power of his thought.

Nevertheless, Buchler's volume is still an excellent, easy to read, and easy to understand (relative to Peirce's depth of thinking) introduction to the immensity of the thought of Charles Peirce. I recommend it as a great reading value.

title: Not Indestructible, but a Great Value
text:
Our shiba loves these toys. For small dogs (20-25lbs), shibas are notoriously rough and tumble players, with the ability to tear through a cold turkey in a matter of minutes (or so one popular breeder/trainer attests from personal experience). So, imagine what they can do to their toys!

Our girl is relatively (key word, here!) calm for a shiba. She never touches anything that isn't hers, but she can get the crazies and do a number on her toys. Tug-of-war is her davorite game, after all, and these are made for it. So, the fact that these are stuffingless is reassuring. She will sometimes tear the ears off of the foxes, but it's from over-time wear-and-tear. She will eventually rip the giant one up (high-energy breeds of any size above a toy breed will need the jumbo), but it will last long enough to be worth the ten or so dollars.

Bottom line, I very much recommend these for all but the most destructive of dogs. The only reason I am not giving five stars is due to the fact that they do eventually wear down, but the low price makes this tolerable. The only other critique I have is that the animal you get seems random, with no visible way to request one over another (our girl really prefers the fox).

There is 2 reasons I don't give this saw 5 stars. First, I haven't used it yet. Second is the wing nut that holds the blade to the handle during use and keeps the saw together when folded and stowed. There is nothing that stops the wing nut from loosening up and potentially falling off and getting lost. I drilled a hole in 1 wing of the wing nut and a hole in the threaded shaft and use a piece of wire threaded through both to keep the wing nut on the rod and not get lost while folded up and traveling. That's its only real drawback. If you loose that wing nut and don't have another, the saw is nearly useless.

text:
The chief delight of this book, and there are many, is that Cunningham has tailored a page-turning, oh-no-don't-do-that!, classic plot of confused identity (i.e. a Comedy of Errors) onto a cutting-edge New York scene, and delivered it with humor, humanity, and depth in a style that is fashionable, highly entertaining, and sexy on the one hand, and deeply poetic on the other, as in he has maybe been reading not only the Bard but that other bard, James Merrill. The characters are sharply drawn both in body and mind, and the plot twists true to both life and character.
Other reviewers are complaining about over-writing. While this may be a bit like grousing that chocolate is rich, Cunningham does stumble here and there, e.g. when he has his hero/narrator say, 'What did Shakespeare say? Our little lives are rounded by a sleep.' This is artificial; Shakespeare himself would have solved the problem by giving that line to the college-student daughter, maybe upon seeing her father drinking vodka in the night!
I think Cunningham has just hit his stride--fine as his past achievements are. Hooray for that! Now lay The Tempest aside, Sir, take up your wand and book, and play, play, play for us!

text:
I bought this padel racket after reading a few budget-friendly recommendations and having only played a handful of times before. For the price, it’s really well made — the finish looks clean, the handle feels solid, and the weight distribution is comfortable for my swing. I’ve played about a dozen matches with it now and it has held up well: no chips or visible wear on the face, and the grip hasn’t loosened or torn. It’s responsive and gives a good balance between control and power, which has helped me improve my volleys and serves.

That said, there are a couple of things to be aware of. First, the racket is a bit stiffer than I expected, so if you’re used to very flexible frames you might notice less forgiveness on off-center hits. It’s not a dealbreaker, but it did take a few sessions to adjust. Second, the included cover is pretty thin — it protects from dust but won’t do much for accidental drops or if you toss it into a crowded car trunk with other gear. I bought a padded case separately.

Overall I’m happy with this purchase. It offers excellent value: sturdy construction, pleasant feel, and solid performance for recreational players and intermediate hobbyists. If you want pro-level specs or top-tier shock absorption, look higher up the price range, but for casual play this is a smart pick.

I must now search for another product that might suit my needs, or try to find an old box on ebay - which is always a gamble, and not a permanent solution.

I miss the old days wear quality mattered - I can't buy a children's game, or even a t-shirt - that has any quality craftsmanship about it. I'm really tired of cheap and crappy stuff.

title: High Adrenaline Thriller with quirks
text:
Music Notes is Manning Wolfe's second installation in the Texas Lady Lawyer series. It's a fast-paced, intense thriller with an eclectic cast, one of those stories that will keep you up so late at night you'll need extra coffee in the morning. Merit Bridges, the perky but powerful protagonist and her quirky team of paralegals find themselves, yet again, in opposition to a deliciously delusional villain intent on their demise.
When the rehabilitated rock guitar hero, Liam Nolan, is brutally murdered with his own guitar, Merit is not only responsible for his estate but feels morally obligated to help solve the crime. Enter Davey Ray Bell who claims to be Liam's love child. Though Davey seems lost and alone there may be some validity to his claim. Meanwhile, Liam's former manager, L A Baron, hopes to grab all the glory and the cash. When he fails to convince the legal authorities of his claim to the riches, he uses his vast resources to attempt to destroy Merit's career and reputation.
The writing is very visual and personal. Wolfe's characters are complex and for the most part driven by more than just material gain. Though the story is definitely dark, it's handled with a quirky humor and panache that brings this storyteller to the pinnacle of legal thriller authors. As an extra bonus, it's set in Austin Texas where the old hippie culture still clashes with the techno-boom of the early 21st century. Wolfe's Texas Lady Lawyer stories scream to be made into a Showtime summer miniseries featuring Reese Witherspoon and her ponytail as the protagonist. Check your local listings, but as always read the book first.

title: Disappointing
text:
I really wanted to love this product because of all the positive things I had read online, but my experience has been pretty mediocre. I purchased this for my daily beauty routine hoping it would give me that glow everyone talks about, but after using it consistently for three weeks, I can honestly say the results are underwhelming.

The texture is nice and it applies smoothly without feeling greasy, which is a plus. It also smells pleasant and doesn't irritate my sensitive skin, which is usually a huge concern for me. However, the actual performance is where it falls short. I haven't noticed any significant change in my skin texture or brightness. It feels more like a basic moisturizer than the transformative treatment it is marketed to be.

For the price point, I expected something much more potent. While it isn't a terrible product—it doesn't cause breakouts or feel unpleasant—it simply doesn't deliver on its promises. It is fine for basic maintenance, but if you are looking for a dramatic improvement in your complexion, this probably isn't the one for you. I will finish the bottle since I already paid for it, but I won't be repurchasing it once it's gone. There are plenty of cheaper alternatives on the market that do the exact same thing. It is a decent product, but ultimately disappointing given the hype. I feel like I paid a premium for branding rather than actual results.
